````
Add two financial patterns that compare every execution prefix through the Core library and public CLI: a three-recipient payout and a reserve, partial-spend and refund sequence.

The payout checks four complete prefixes and effects, preserved observer balances and duties, gross debit 25 including fee 2, and logical work 8. Full Program and CLI comparisons retain explicit assumptions about source-specific expression IDs and exact output formatting. The reserve example checks 20 financial prefixes and 17 effects: gross debit stays 100 after refund 20, while the remaining reserve and duty are both 40. Its allowance counters are application state.

Validation on `98db9d3cf7a7e1227fdbbd9e6d5d3c2d848a6453` (tree `6f78f49dc3cc643c423a5c0c4f9d85fa9a0aa09b`): five tests passed, none failed or filtered, in 55.612 seconds. Complete library outcomes and CLI streams were captured before comparisons. The first run failed because the test omitted indices from cumulative-effect records; fixing that adapter preserved every oracle byte. Both runs remain recorded. The checkout stayed clean, temporary files were removed, and diff-check passed. Independent source/result review is pending. Compiler, proof, ledger and whole-family qualification remain open.
````

````
//! Ordinary Core/1 financial prefixes from an independently frozen source case.
use serde_json::{Value, json};
use std::{
    fs,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
    process::Command,
    sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
};

fn fixtures() -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../fixtures/reserve-spend-refund")
}

fn json_file(path: &Path) -> Value {
    serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(path).unwrap()).unwrap()
}

// This selects observable fields; it never computes a financial transition.
// Complete statement/ExprId correspondence remains a separate oracle boundary.
fn financial_execution(execution: &Value) -> Value {
    let steps = execution["steps"]
        .as_array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .map(|step| {
            json!({
                "index": step["index"],
                "value": step["value"],
                "snapshot": step["snapshot"],
                "effects": step["effects"],
            })
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    json!({
        "semantics": execution["semantics"],
        "action": execution["action"],
        "pre": execution["pre"],
        "post": execution["post"],
        "steps": steps,
        "effects": execution["effects"],
    })
}

fn assert_financial_prefixes(execution: &Value) {
    let root = fixtures();
    assert_eq!(
        financial_execution(execution),
        json_file(&root.join("financial-execution-projection.expected.json")),
        "every typed result, changed and preserved row, and new effect delta"
    );
    let kinds = execution["steps"]
        .as_array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .map(|step| step["statement"]["kind"].clone())
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    assert_eq!(
        Value::Array(kinds),
        json_file(&root.join("source-statement-kinds.expected.json")),
        "all source statement kinds, without inventing expression roots"
    );
    let mut prefix = Vec::new();
    let prefixes = execution["steps"]
        .as_array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .map(|step| {
            prefix.extend(step["effects"].as_array().unwrap().iter().cloned());
            Value::Array(prefix.clone())
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    assert_eq!(
        Value::Array(prefixes),
        json_file(&root.join("cumulative-prefix-effects.expected.json")),
        "all ordered effect prefixes against independent literals"
    );
}

#[test]
fn reserve_library_keeps_complete_financial_prefixes() {
    let root = fixtures();
    let source = fs::read_to_string(root.join("reserve-spend-refund.mori")).unwrap();
    let program = mori_core::parse(&source).expect("the ordinary source must parse");
    let scenario =
        serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(root.join("opening.scenario.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let execution = mori_core::simulate(&program, "run", &scenario)
        .expect("the positive reference call must complete");
    assert_financial_prefixes(&serde_json::to_value(execution).unwrap());
}

static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);

struct Project {
    root: PathBuf,
    temporary: bool,
}

impl Project {
    fn new() -> Self {
        let (root, temporary) = match std::env::var_os("MORI_CORE_REFUND_OBSERVATIONS") {
            Some(path) => {
                let path = PathBuf::from(path);
                assert!(path.is_absolute(), "observation path must be absolute");
                (path, false)
            }
            None => (
                std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
                    "mori-reserve-refund-{}-{}",
                    std::process::id(),
                    NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
                )),
                true,
            ),
        };
        fs::create_dir(&root).expect("use a fresh observation directory");
        for name in ["reserve-spend-refund.mori", "opening.scenario.json"] {
            fs::copy(fixtures().join(name), root.join(name)).unwrap();
        }
        Self { root, temporary }
    }
}

impl Drop for Project {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if self.temporary && !std::thread::panicking() {
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.root);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn reserve_public_cli_keeps_complete_financial_prefixes() {
    let project = Project::new();
    let args = [
        "--color",
        "never",
        "simulate",
        "reserve-spend-refund.mori",
        "--action",
        "run",
        "--scenario",
        "opening.scenario.json",
    ];
    let captured = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_mori"))
        .current_dir(&project.root)
        .args(args)
        .output();
    if let Err(error) = &captured {
        fs::write(
            project.root.join("process.json"),
            serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&json!({
                "executable": env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_mori"),
                "args": args,
                "launchError": error.to_string(),
            }))
            .unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap();
    }
    let output = captured.expect("the reviewed public binary must launch");
    // Save complete actual process bytes and outcome before result assertions.
    fs::write(project.root.join("stdout.json"), &output.stdout).unwrap();
    fs::write(project.root.join("stderr.txt"), &output.stderr).unwrap();
    fs::write(
        project.root.join("process.json"),
        serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&json!({
            "executable": env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_mori"),
            "args": args,
            "status": output.status.code(),
            "success": output.status.success(),
        }))
        .unwrap(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(output.status.code(), Some(0));
    assert!(output.stderr.is_empty());
    let report: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&output.stdout).unwrap();
    let mut keys = report
        .as_object()
        .unwrap()
        .keys()
        .map(String::as_str)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    keys.sort_unstable();
    assert_eq!(keys, ["execution", "qualification", "status"]);
    assert_eq!(report["status"], "accepted");
    assert_eq!(report["qualification"], "local-reference-execution");
    assert_financial_prefixes(&report["execution"]);
}
````

````
use std::process::ExitCode;

use clap::Parser;

use crate::cli::Cli;
use crate::shell::Shell;

mod cli;
mod commands;
mod display;
mod error;
mod json;
mod shell;
mod styles;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let cli = Cli::parse();
    let mut shell = Shell::new(cli.global.verbosity(), cli.global.color.into());

    match commands::run(cli.command, &mut shell) {
        Ok(code) => code,
        Err(report) => {
            shell.report(&report);
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}
````

````
use std::path::PathBuf;

use clap::{Args, Parser, Subcommand, ValueEnum};

use crate::commands::{
    capabilities, check, compile, compile_call, expand, format, init, inspect, intent, keygen_call,
    keygen_signed_call, lsp, mcp, prepare_call, prepare_signed_call, prove, prove_call,
    prove_signed_call, replay, simulate, test, verify, verify_call, verify_intent,
    verify_signed_call,
};
use crate::shell::Verbosity;
use crate::styles;

/// Moriarty: a financial agreement language for Midnight.
#[derive(Debug, Parser)]
#[command(name = "mori", version, styles = styles::CLAP)]
#[cfg_attr(
    all(not(feature = "native"), not(feature = "source6-expansion")),
    command(
        after_help = "Built without native: local Core reference tooling only. Midnight compile, call, proof, targeted inspect, trace/replay and JubJub profiles require the native feature."
    )
)]
#[cfg_attr(
    all(not(feature = "native"), feature = "source6-expansion"),
    command(
        after_help = "Built without native: local Core reference tooling and explicit Source/6 transfer expansion only. Midnight compile, call, proof, targeted inspect, trace/replay and JubJub profiles require the native feature."
    )
)]
pub struct Cli {
    #[command(flatten)]
    pub global: GlobalArgs,

    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: Command,
}

#[derive(Debug, Args)]
#[command(next_help_heading = "Global Options")]
pub struct GlobalArgs {
    /// Print no status output
    #[arg(short, long, global = true, conflicts_with = "verbose")]
    pub quiet: bool,

    /// Print extra status output
    #[arg(short, long, global = true)]
    pub verbose: bool,

    /// When to use color
    #[arg(long, global = true, value_name = "WHEN", default_value = "auto")]
    pub color: Color,
}

impl GlobalArgs {
    pub fn verbosity(&self) -> Verbosity {
        if self.quiet {
            Verbosity::Quiet
        } else if self.verbose {
            Verbosity::Verbose
        } else {
            Verbosity::Normal
        }
    }
}

/// Selects one action of an agreement and the scenario to run it against.
#[derive(Debug, Args)]
pub struct ActionInput {
    /// Source file
    pub file: PathBuf,

    /// Action to run
    #[arg(long, value_name = "NAME")]
    pub action: String,

    /// Scenario JSON with the local state and inputs
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE")]
    pub scenario: PathBuf,
}

/// Output format for the signing commands.
#[derive(Debug, Args)]
pub struct SigningOutputArgs {
    /// Print a human review of what is being signed or verified
    #[arg(long, conflicts_with = "json")]
    pub review: bool,

    /// Print the result as JSON
    #[arg(long)]
    pub json: bool,
}

/// Signed native owner-intent profile selected explicitly by name.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, ValueEnum)]
pub enum SignedProfile {
    #[value(name = "moriarty-jubjub-owner-intent/1")]
    JubjubOwnerIntent,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, ValueEnum)]
pub enum Color {
    Auto,
    Always,
    Never,
}

impl From<Color> for anstream::ColorChoice {
    fn from(color: Color) -> Self {
        match color {
            Color::Auto => Self::Auto,
            Color::Always => Self::Always,
            Color::Never => Self::Never,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Subcommand)]
pub enum Command {
    /// Describe compiled features and public source consumers without running them
    Capabilities(capabilities::Args),
    /// Create a new project from a starter template
    Init(init::Args),
    /// Check syntax, names, types and action support
    Check(check::Args),
    /// Compile a bounded Moriarty program into ledger-9 ZKIRv3 circuits
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    Compile(compile::Args),
    /// Compile a source-static ordinary native contract-call relation
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    CompileCall(compile_call::Args),
    /// Derive all source action keys and an explicit local installed snapshot
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    KeygenCall(keygen_call::Args),
    /// Derive the complete local signed action map under a fixed JubJub policy
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    KeygenSignedCall(keygen_signed_call::Args),
    /// Reconstruct a signature-free canonical local call signing package
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    PrepareSignedCall(prepare_signed_call::Args),
    /// Prove the actual local typed SDK call with an external FENS attachment
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    ProveSignedCall(prove_signed_call::Args),
    /// Cold public-only reconstruction and Real verification of a signed call
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    VerifySignedCall(verify_signed_call::Args),
    /// Cold rederive keys and prove an actual local installed SDK call
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    ProveCall(prove_call::Args),
    /// Cold rederive public keys and Real-verify an installed call without PK files
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    VerifyCall(verify_call::Args),
    /// Prove a public local action using pinned offline parameters
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    Prove(prove::Args),
    /// Prepare an unsigned, unproven local native call and public offer
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    PrepareCall(prepare_call::Args),
    /// Verify a native proof against the expected source, target and scenario
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    Verify(verify::Args),
    /// Format source files in place
    #[command(visible_alias = "fmt")]
    Format(format::Args),
    /// Show identity claims, operative bounds and open premises
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Without native, source-only inspection is available; --target requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    Inspect(inspect::Args),
    /// Show the native core IR after checking an action against a scenario
    Expand(expand::Args),
    /// Run an action locally against a scenario
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Without native, local Core simulation and staged start/resume are available; --trace requires the native feature."
        )
    )]
    Simulate(simulate::Args),
    /// Independently replay a public record against separately trusted inputs
    #[cfg_attr(
        not(feature = "native"),
        command(
            after_help = "Unavailable in this build: this command requires the native feature."
        )
````

````
//! One module per subcommand. Each defines its `Args` and a `run` function.

use std::process::ExitCode;

use mori_diagnostics::Report;

use crate::cli::Command;
use crate::shell::Shell;

mod call_io;
pub mod capabilities;
pub mod check;
pub mod compile;
pub mod compile_call;
mod core_io;
pub mod expand;
pub mod format;
pub mod init;
pub mod inspect;
pub mod intent;
pub mod keygen_call;
pub mod keygen_signed_call;
pub mod lsp;
pub mod mcp;
pub mod prepare_call;
pub mod prepare_signed_call;
mod proof_io;
pub mod prove;
pub mod prove_call;
pub mod prove_signed_call;
pub mod replay;
mod signed_call_io;
pub mod simulate;
pub mod test;
pub mod verify;
pub mod verify_call;
pub mod verify_intent;
pub mod verify_signed_call;

pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Report>;

pub fn run(command: Command, shell: &mut Shell) -> Result<ExitCode> {
    match command {
        Command::Capabilities(args) => capabilities::run(args, shell),
        Command::Init(args) => init::run(args, shell),
        Command::Check(args) => check::run(args, shell),
        Command::Compile(args) => compile::run(args, shell),
        Command::KeygenSignedCall(args) => keygen_signed_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::PrepareSignedCall(args) => prepare_signed_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::ProveSignedCall(args) => prove_signed_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::VerifySignedCall(args) => verify_signed_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::KeygenCall(args) => keygen_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::ProveCall(args) => prove_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::VerifyCall(args) => verify_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::CompileCall(args) => compile_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::PrepareCall(args) => prepare_call::run(args, shell),
        Command::Prove(args) => prove::run(args, shell),
        Command::Verify(args) => verify::run(args, shell),
        Command::Format(args) => format::run(args, shell),
        Command::Inspect(args) => inspect::run(args, shell),
        Command::Expand(args) => expand::run(args, shell),
        Command::Simulate(args) => simulate::run(args, shell),
        Command::Replay(args) => replay::run(args, shell),
        Command::Test(args) => test::run(args, shell),
        Command::Intent(args) => intent::run(args, shell),
        Command::VerifyIntent(args) => verify_intent::run(args, shell),
        Command::Lsp(args) => lsp::run(args, shell),
        Command::Mcp(args) => mcp::run(args, shell),
    }
}

#[cfg(not(feature = "native"))]
fn native_unavailable<T>() -> Result<T> {
    Err(crate::error::CliError::Operation {
        code: "mori::command::native-unavailable".into(),
        message: "This mori build has no Midnight support. Rebuild with the native feature enabled."
            .into(),
    }
    .into())
}
````

````
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::ExitCode;

use crate::shell::Shell;

#[derive(Debug, clap::Args)]
pub struct Args {
    /// Source file
    pub file: PathBuf,

    /// Action to run
    #[arg(long, value_name = "NAME", required_unless_present = "resume")]
    pub action: Option<String>,

    /// Scenario JSON with the local state and inputs
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE", required_unless_present = "resume")]
    pub scenario: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Resume a moriarty/2 continuation (local, unauthenticated, consumption untracked)
    #[arg(
        long,
        value_name = "FILE",
        requires = "event",
        conflicts_with_all = ["scenario", "trace", "target", "profile", "authority", "at", "signature"]
    )]
    pub resume: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Stage event JSON for --resume (at most 64 KiB)
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE", requires = "resume")]
    pub event: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Generate a complete public replay sidecar against a trusted Target
    #[arg(long)]
    pub trace: bool,
    /// Cap local statement and uncached expression attempts (other costs unmeasured)
    #[arg(long, value_name = "CANONICAL_U128", value_parser = logical_cap, conflicts_with = "trace")]
    pub logical_cap: Option<mori_core::UInt>,
    /// Trusted Target JSON (required with --trace)
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE")]
    pub target: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    #[command(flatten)]
    pub authorization: super::replay::AuthorizationArgs,
}

impl Args {
    /// Legacy start inputs. Clap requires both whenever --resume is absent.
    fn legacy(&self) -> super::Result<(&str, &Path)> {
        match (self.action.as_deref(), self.scenario.as_deref()) {
            (Some(action), Some(scenario)) => Ok((action, scenario)),
            _ => Err(super::core_io::operation(
                "--action and --scenario are required without --resume",
            )),
        }
    }
}

fn logical_cap(value: &str) -> Result<mori_core::UInt, String> {
    serde_json::from_value(serde_json::Value::String(value.into()))
        .map_err(|_| "expected canonical unsigned decimal string in u128 range".into())
}

pub fn run(args: Args, _shell: &mut Shell) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    // Clap has already refused every --resume/--event conflict, so a
    // malformed invocation reads no file.
    if let Some(resume) = &args.resume {
        return run_resume(&args, resume);
    }
    let (action, scenario_path) = args.legacy()?;
    if args.trace {
        let path = args
            .target
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| super::core_io::operation("--trace requires --target"))?;
        #[cfg(feature = "native")]
        let target = super::core_io::read_json(path)?;
        #[cfg(feature = "native")]
        let authorization = args.authorization.load(&target)?;
        #[cfg(feature = "native")]
        let source = super::core_io::read_source(&args.file)?;
        #[cfg(feature = "native")]
        let scenario = super::core_io::read_json(scenario_path)?;
        #[cfg(feature = "native")]
        return match mori_backend::replay::generate(
            &source,
            action,
            &scenario,
            &target,
            authorization.as_input(),
        ) {
            Ok(record) => {
                super::core_io::print(&record)?;
                Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
            }
            Err(error) => {
                super::core_io::print(
                    &serde_json::json!({"status":"rejected","qualification":"local-reference-replay","error":error}),
                )?;
                Ok(ExitCode::FAILURE)
            }
        };
        #[cfg(not(feature = "native"))]
        {
            let _ = path;
            return super::native_unavailable();
        }
    }
    if args.target.is_some() || args.authorization.present() {
        return Err(super::core_io::operation(
            "--target and signed replay arguments require --trace",
        ));
    }
    let source = super::core_io::read_source(&args.file)?;
    // Hook: /2 routing. A /2 start keeps every core failure labelled.
    if mori_core::language(&source) == Ok(mori_core::stage::LANGUAGE_2) {
        return run_stage_start(&args, &source, action, scenario_path);
    }
    let program = mori_core::parse(&source).map_err(super::core_io::operation)?;
    let scenario = super::core_io::read_json(scenario_path)?;
    if let Some(cap) = args.logical_cap {
        return match mori_core::simulate_metered(&program, action, &scenario, cap) {
            Ok(metered) => {
                super::core_io::print(&serde_json::json!({
                    "status": "accepted", "qualification": "local-reference-execution",
                    "execution": metered.execution, "profile": metered.cost.profile,
                    "logical": {"cap": metered.cost.cap, "used": metered.cost.used}
                }))?;
                Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
            }
            Err(refused) => {
                super::core_io::print(&serde_json::json!({
                    "status": "rejected", "error": refused.error,
                    "profile": refused.cost.profile,
                    "logical": {"cap": refused.cost.cap, "used": refused.cost.used}
                }))?;
                Ok(ExitCode::FAILURE)
            }
        };
    }
    match mori_core::simulate(&program, action, &scenario) {
        Ok(execution) => {
            super::core_io::print(
                &serde_json::json!({"status":"accepted", "qualification":"local-reference-execution", "execution":execution}),
            )?;
            Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
        }
        Err(error) => {
            super::core_io::print(&serde_json::json!({"status":"rejected", "error":error}))?;
            Ok(ExitCode::FAILURE)
        }
    }
}

/// Render the same explicit qualification on every staged public object.
pub(super) fn print_stage_report(mut report: serde_json::Value) -> super::Result<()> {
    let object = report
        .as_object_mut()
        .expect("stage reports are JSON objects");
    for (name, value) in mori_core::stage::STAGE_LABELS {
        object.insert(name.into(), serde_json::Value::String(value.into()));
    }
    super::core_io::print(&report)
}

fn print_stage_result(
    result: Result<mori_core::stage::StageOutcome, mori_core::stage::StageRejection>,
) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    let exit = if result.is_ok() {
        ExitCode::SUCCESS
    } else {
        ExitCode::FAILURE
    };
    super::core_io::print(&mori_core::stage::outcome_report(result))?;
    Ok(exit)
}

/// `--resume`: reads the source, then the continuation, then the event.
/// Bounded-read, strict-decode, load and admission failures are labelled stage
/// rejections; a source the filesystem cannot read keeps the legacy error.
/// Nothing is recorded, so the same file can be resumed again (untracked).
fn run_resume(args: &Args, resume: &Path) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    use mori_core::stage::{self, StageOutcome, StageRejection, decode};
    let event_path = args
        .event
        .as_deref()
        .ok_or_else(|| super::core_io::operation("--resume requires --event"))?;
    let source = super::core_io::read_source(&args.file)?;
    let result = (|| -> Result<StageOutcome, StageRejection> {
        let program = stage::load(&source).map_err(no_work)?;
        let continuation = decode::read_bounded(
            resume,
            decode::MAX_CONTINUATION_BYTES,
            decode::CONTINUATION_TOO_LARGE,
        )
        .and_then(|text| decode::continuation(&text))
        .map_err(no_work)?;
        let event =
            decode::read_bounded(event_path, decode::MAX_EVENT_BYTES, decode::EVENT_TOO_LARGE)
                .and_then(|text| decode::event(&text))
                .map_err(no_work)?;
        stage::resume(
            &program,
            continuation,
            event,
            args.action.as_deref(),
            args.logical_cap,
        )
    })();
    print_stage_result(result)
}

/// A `/2` start. Load and scenario failures are labelled stage rejections; the
/// scenario keeps the legacy 1 MiB strict reader.
fn run_stage_start(
    args: &Args,
    source: &str,
    action: &str,
    scenario: &Path,
) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    use mori_core::stage::{self, StageOutcome, StageRejection, decode};
    let result = (|| -> Result<StageOutcome, StageRejection> {
        let program = stage::load(source).map_err(no_work)?;
        let text = decode::read_bounded(scenario, 1_048_576, "Scenario JSON exceeds 1 MiB")
            .map_err(no_work)?;
        let value = mori_core::json::parse(&text).map_err(no_work)?;
        let scenario = serde_json::from_value(value).map_err(|error| {
            no_work(mori_core::Error {
                code: "mori::core::json".into(),
                message: error.to_string(),
                offset: None,
                step: None,
            })
        })?;
        stage::start(&program, action, scenario, args.logical_cap)
    })();
    print_stage_result(result)
}

/// A refusal before any segment evaluation: no work attempted or committed.
fn no_work(error: mori_core::Error) -> mori_core::stage::StageRejection {
    mori_core::stage::StageRejection {
        error,
        attempted: mori_core::UInt(0),
        committed: mori_core::UInt(0),
    }
}
````

````
//! Actual CLI replay consumer; all roots and signature attachment are separate inputs.
use crate::{
    cli::{ActionInput, SignedProfile},
    shell::Shell,
};
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
use mori_backend::{
    Target,
    authorization::{ExpectedAuthority, SignedIntent},
    replay::{ReplayAuthorization, ReplayError, ReplayRecord},
};
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
use mori_core::UInt;
use std::{path::PathBuf, process::ExitCode};

#[derive(Debug, clap::Args, Default)]
pub struct AuthorizationArgs {
    /// Strict signed owner-intent profile (signed Targets require the complete group)
    #[arg(long)]
    pub profile: Option<SignedProfile>,
    /// Separately trusted expected account/domain authority
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE")]
    pub authority: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// Separately trusted logical time (not authenticated ledger time)
    #[arg(long)]
    pub at: Option<u128>,
    /// Actual external signed wrapper; never loaded from the record
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE")]
    pub signature: Option<PathBuf>,
}
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub enum LoadedAuthorization {
    Unsigned,
    Signed {
        authority: Box<ExpectedAuthority>,
        at: UInt,
        signature: Box<SignedIntent>,
    },
}
impl AuthorizationArgs {
    pub fn present(&self) -> bool {
        self.profile.is_some()
            || self.authority.is_some()
            || self.at.is_some()
            || self.signature.is_some()
    }
    #[cfg(feature = "native")]
    pub fn load(&self, target: &Target) -> super::Result<LoadedAuthorization> {
        if target.signed_policy.is_none() {
            if self.present() {
                return Err(super::core_io::operation(
                    "Signed replay arguments require a trusted Target with signed_policy",
                ));
            }
            return Ok(LoadedAuthorization::Unsigned);
        }
        let (Some(_), Some(authority), Some(at), Some(signature)) =
            (&self.profile, &self.authority, self.at, &self.signature)
        else {
            return Err(super::core_io::operation(
                "Signed Target requires --profile moriarty-jubjub-owner-intent/1, --authority, --at and --signature together",
            ));
        };
        Ok(LoadedAuthorization::Signed {
            authority: Box::new(super::core_io::authority(authority)?),
            at: UInt(at),
            signature: Box::new(super::core_io::signed_intent(signature)?),
        })
    }
}
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
impl LoadedAuthorization {
    pub fn as_input(&self) -> ReplayAuthorization<'_> {
        match self {
            Self::Unsigned => ReplayAuthorization::Unsigned,
            Self::Signed {
                authority,
                at,
                signature,
            } => ReplayAuthorization::Signed {
                authority,
                at: *at,
                signature,
            },
        }
    }
}
#[derive(Debug, clap::Args)]
pub struct Args {
    #[command(flatten)]
    pub input: ActionInput,
    /// Separately trusted Target JSON
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE")]
    pub target: PathBuf,
    /// Public sidecar to compare; never supplies trusted roots
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE")]
    pub record: PathBuf,
    /// Export a bounded local first-divergence diagnostic to a new file
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE")]
    pub challenge_out: Option<PathBuf>,
    #[command(flatten)]
    pub authorization: AuthorizationArgs,
}
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub fn run(args: Args, _shell: &mut Shell) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    // File/schema/group errors have the same input classification as failed
    // reconstruction. Neither case creates or publishes a challenge.
    let inputs = (|| {
        let target = super::core_io::read_json(&args.target)?;
        let authorization = args.authorization.load(&target)?;
        let candidate = ReplayRecord::from_json(&super::core_io::read_source(&args.record)?)
            .map_err(super::core_io::operation)?;
        let source = super::core_io::read_source(&args.input.file)?;
        let scenario = super::core_io::read_json(&args.input.scenario)?;
        Ok::<_, mori_diagnostics::Report>((target, authorization, candidate, source, scenario))
    })();
    let (target, authorization, candidate, source, scenario) = match inputs {
        Ok(inputs) => inputs,
        Err(error) => {
            super::core_io::print(
                &serde_json::json!({"status":"rejected","qualification":"local-reference-replay","error":{"kind":"input","detail":error.to_string()}}),
            )?;
            return Ok(ExitCode::FAILURE);
        }
    };
    let result = mori_backend::replay::challenge(
        &source,
        &args.input.action,
        &scenario,
        &target,
        authorization.as_input(),
        &candidate,
    );
    let (report, status) = match result {
        // Successful full equality includes independently reconstructed record_hash.
        Ok(None) => (
            serde_json::json!({"status":"accepted","qualification":"local-reference-replay","record_hash":candidate.record_hash}),
            ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        ),
        Ok(Some(challenge)) => {
            let d = &challenge.divergence;
            if let Some(path) = &args.challenge_out {
                let published = challenge
                    .to_json()
                    .map_err(super::core_io::operation)
                    .and_then(|text| {
                        super::proof_io::publish_new(path, format!("{text}\n").as_bytes())
                    });
                if let Err(error) = published {
                    super::core_io::print(
                        &serde_json::json!({"status":"rejected","qualification":"local-reference-replay","error":{"kind":"output","detail":error.to_string()},"divergence":d}),
                    )?;
                    return Ok(ExitCode::FAILURE);
                }
            }
            (
                serde_json::json!({"status":"rejected","qualification":"local-reference-replay","error":{"kind":"divergence","step":d.step,"field":d.field}}),
                ExitCode::FAILURE,
            )
        }
        Err(ReplayError::Input(error)) => (
            serde_json::json!({"status":"rejected","qualification":"local-reference-replay","error":{"kind":"input","detail":error}}),
            ExitCode::FAILURE,
        ),
        // challenge converts semantic divergence to a diagnostic. Preserve an
        // explicit refusal if that API ever gains another divergence branch.
        Err(ReplayError::Divergence(d)) => (
            serde_json::json!({"status":"rejected","qualification":"local-reference-replay","error":{"kind":"divergence","step":d.step,"field":d.field}}),
            ExitCode::FAILURE,
        ),
    };
    super::core_io::print(&report)?;
    Ok(status)
}

#[cfg(not(feature = "native"))]
pub fn run(args: Args, _shell: &mut Shell) -> super::Result<ExitCode> {
    let _ = (
        &args.input,
        &args.target,
        &args.record,
        &args.challenge_out,
        &args.authorization,
    );
    super::native_unavailable()
}
````

````
use crate::error::CliError;
use serde::{Serialize, de::DeserializeOwned};
use std::path::Path;

pub fn read_source(path: &Path) -> super::Result<String> {
    use std::io::Read;
    let file = std::fs::File::open(path).map_err(|source| CliError::Read {
        path: path.into(),
        source,
    })?;
    let mut source = String::new();
    file.take(1_048_577)
        .read_to_string(&mut source)
        .map_err(|source| CliError::Read {
            path: path.into(),
            source,
        })?;
    if source.len() > 1_048_576 {
        return Err(operation("input file exceeds 1 MiB"));
    }
    Ok(source)
}

#[cfg(all(test, feature = "native"))]
mod key_export_diagnostic_tests {
    use super::*;
    use mori_ledger::{Error, KeyExportDiagnostic, KeyExportFailureReason, KeyExportKind};

    fn refusal(action: &str, key_kind: KeyExportKind, reason: KeyExportFailureReason) -> Error {
        let cap_refusal = reason == KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded;
        Error::new("native-proving", "generated-key-size-or-encode").with_key_export(
            KeyExportDiagnostic {
                action: action.into(),
                key_kind,
                discovered_degree: 0,
                byte_cap: 3,
                accepted_bytes: 2,
                failed_write_bytes: (reason != KeyExportFailureReason::Serialization).then_some(2),
                attempted_minimum: cap_refusal.then_some(4),
                reason,
            },
        )
    }
    #[test]
    fn key_export_cli_preserves_category_and_discriminates_reasons() {
        for kind in [KeyExportKind::Prover, KeyExportKind::Verifier] {
            for (reason, label) in [
                (KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded, "byte-cap-exceeded"),
                (
                    KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCountOverflow,
                    "byte-count-overflow",
                ),
                (
                    KeyExportFailureReason::Serialization,
                    "serialization-failure",
                ),
            ] {
                let report = ledger_operation(refusal("settle", kind, reason)).to_string();
                let kind = if kind == KeyExportKind::Prover {
                    "prover"
                } else {
                    "verifier"
                };
                assert!(report.starts_with("mori::command: mori::ledger::native-proving: generated-key-size-or-encode; "), "{report}");
                assert!(report.contains(&format!("action=\"settle\" key-kind={kind} discovered-degree=0 byte-cap=3 accepted-bytes=2 reason={label}")), "{report}");
                assert_eq!(
                    report.contains("failed-write-bytes=2"),
                    reason != KeyExportFailureReason::Serialization
                );
                assert_eq!(
                    report.contains("attempted-minimum=4"),
                    reason == KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded
                );
            }
        }
        let legacy = Error::new("native-proving", "sdk-keygen");
        assert_eq!(
            ledger_operation(legacy.clone()).to_string(),
            operation(legacy).to_string()
        );
    }
    #[test]
    fn key_export_cli_action_is_ascii_json_escaped_once_and_round_trips() {
        let action = "settle\"\\\nforged\r\u{1b}[31m\u{7f}\u{85}\u{202e}\u{1f9ea}";
        let error = refusal(
            action,
            KeyExportKind::Verifier,
            KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded,
        );
        assert_eq!(error.key_export().unwrap().action, action);
        let report = ledger_operation(error).to_string();
        let encoded = report
            .split_once("; action=")
            .unwrap()
            .1
            .split_once(" key-kind=")
            .unwrap()
            .0;
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<String>(encoded).unwrap(), action);
        assert!(report.is_ascii(), "{report}");
        assert!(report.chars().all(|c| !c.is_control()), "{report}");
        assert!(encoded.contains(r"\u0085"));
        assert!(encoded.contains(r"\u202e"));
        assert!(encoded.contains(r"\ud83e\uddea"));
        assert_eq!(
            encoded,
            r#""settle\"\\\nforged\r\u001b[31m\u007f\u0085\u202e\ud83e\uddea""#
        );
    }
    #[test]
    fn key_export_quiet_shell_reports_safe_metadata_on_actual_stderr() {
        const CHILD: &str = "MORI_KEY_EXPORT_DIAGNOSTIC_REPORT_CHILD";
        if std::env::var_os(CHILD).is_some() {
            let report = ledger_operation(refusal(
                "settle\n\u{1b}\u{202e}",
                KeyExportKind::Prover,
                KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded,
            ));
            let mut shell = crate::shell::Shell::new(
                crate::shell::Verbosity::Quiet,
                anstream::ColorChoice::Never,
            );
            shell.report(&report);
            return;
        }
        let output = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
            .args(["--exact", "commands::core_io::key_export_diagnostic_tests::key_export_quiet_shell_reports_safe_metadata_on_actual_stderr", "--nocapture"])
            .env(CHILD, "1").output().unwrap();
        assert!(output.status.success());
        let stderr = String::from_utf8(output.stderr).unwrap();
        // The trusted renderer adds Unicode box drawing and may wrap a field
        // across lines. Inspect its joined content, plus raw hostile controls.
        let content: String = stderr
            .lines()
            .map(|line| {
                line.strip_prefix("  │ ")
                    .or_else(|| line.strip_prefix("  × "))
                    .unwrap_or(line)
            })
            .collect();
        for value in [
            "generated-key-size-or-encode",
            "key-kind=prover",
            "discovered-degree=0",
            "byte-cap=3",
            "accepted-bytes=2",
            "byte-cap-exceeded",
            "failed-write-bytes=2",
            "attempted-minimum=4",
            r#"action="settle\n\u001b\u202e""#,
        ] {
            assert!(content.contains(value), "{stderr}");
        }
        assert!(!stderr.contains(['\u{1b}', '\u{85}', '\u{202e}']));
        assert!(!stderr.contains("key-bytes"));
    }
}
pub fn operation(error: impl std::fmt::Display) -> mori_diagnostics::Report {
    CliError::Operation {
        code: "mori::command".into(),
        message: crate::display::text(&error.to_string()),
    }
    .into()
}
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub fn ledger_operation(error: mori_ledger::Error) -> mori_diagnostics::Report {
    use mori_ledger::{DegreeRefusalReason, KeyExportFailureReason, KeyExportKind};
    let mut message = crate::display::text(&error.to_string());
    if let Some(diagnostic) = error.degree_refusal() {
        let reason = match diagnostic.reason {
            DegreeRefusalReason::CallerCeilingExceeded => "caller-ceiling-exceeded",
            DegreeRefusalReason::UnsupportedPinnedDegree => "unsupported-pinned-degree",
            DegreeRefusalReason::CachedDegreeMismatch { .. } => "cached-degree-mismatch",
        };
        // Quote the exact source identity once; operation() would escape this
        // already-rendered identity again. All remaining context is metadata.
        message.push_str(&format!(
            "; action={} discovered-degree={} caller-ceiling={} pinned-supported={} reason={reason}",
            review_identity(&diagnostic.action),
            diagnostic.discovered_degree,
            diagnostic.caller_ceiling,
            diagnostic.pinned_supported,
        ));
        if let DegreeRefusalReason::CachedDegreeMismatch { cached_degree } = diagnostic.reason {
            message.push_str(&format!(" cached-degree={cached_degree}"));
        }
    }
    if let Some(diagnostic) = error.key_export() {
        let kind = match diagnostic.key_kind {
            KeyExportKind::Prover => "prover",
            KeyExportKind::Verifier => "verifier",
        };
        let reason = match diagnostic.reason {
            KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCapExceeded => "byte-cap-exceeded",
            KeyExportFailureReason::ByteCountOverflow => "byte-count-overflow",
            KeyExportFailureReason::Serialization => "serialization-failure",
        };
        message.push_str(&format!(
            "; action={} key-kind={kind} discovered-degree={} byte-cap={} accepted-bytes={} reason={reason}",
            key_export_identity(&diagnostic.action),
            diagnostic.discovered_degree,
            diagnostic.byte_cap,
            diagnostic.accepted_bytes,
        ));
        if let Some(bytes) = diagnostic.failed_write_bytes {
            message.push_str(&format!(" failed-write-bytes={bytes}"));
        }
        if let Some(minimum) = diagnostic.attempted_minimum {
            message.push_str(&format!(" attempted-minimum={minimum}"));
        }
    }
    CliError::Operation {
        code: "mori::command".into(),
        message,
    }
    .into()
}
/// JSON escaping quotes/controls once, with UTF-16 escapes for non-ASCII
/// identities. This remains valid JSON even for supplementary Unicode scalars.
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
fn key_export_identity(value: &str) -> String {
    let json = serde_json::to_string(value).expect("serializing a string cannot fail");
    let mut escaped = String::with_capacity(json.len());
    for character in json.chars() {
        if character.is_ascii() && !character.is_control() {
            escaped.push(character);
        } else {
            let mut units = [0; 2];
            for unit in character.encode_utf16(&mut units) {
                use std::fmt::Write;
                write!(escaped, "\\u{unit:04x}").expect("writing to a String cannot fail");
            }
        }
    }
    escaped
}
pub fn read_json<T: DeserializeOwned>(path: &Path) -> super::Result<T> {
    let source = read_source(path)?;
    let value = mori_core::json::parse(&source).map_err(operation)?;
    serde_json::from_value(value).map_err(operation)
}
pub fn program(path: &Path) -> super::Result<(String, mori_core::Program)> {
    let source = read_source(path)?;
    let program = mori_core::parse(&source).map_err(operation)?;
    Ok((source, program))
}
pub fn print<T: Serialize>(value: &T) -> super::Result<()> {
    let display = mori_core::json::export(value).map_err(operation)?;
    println!("{display}");
    Ok(())
}
/// Trusted signed Target, separately supplied expected authority and logical time.
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub fn signed_target(path: &Path) -> super::Result<mori_backend::Target> {
    let target: mori_backend::Target = read_json(path)?;
    if target.signed_policy.is_none() {
        return Err(operation(
            "the signed profile requires a trusted Target with signed_policy",
        ));
    }
    Ok(target)
}
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub fn authority(path: &Path) -> super::Result<mori_backend::authorization::ExpectedAuthority> {
    mori_backend::authorization::ExpectedAuthority::from_json(&read_source(path)?)
        .map_err(operation)
}
#[cfg(feature = "native")]
pub fn signed_intent(path: &Path) -> super::Result<mori_backend::authorization::SignedIntent> {
    mori_backend::authorization::SignedIntent::from_json(&read_source(path)?).map_err(operation)
}
/// Quote display identities without giving source text terminal control.
pub fn review_identity(value: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "\"{}\"",
        value
            .chars()
            .flat_map(char::escape_default)
            .collect::<String>()
    )
}

#[cfg(all(test, feature = "native"))]
mod degree_diagnostic_tests {
    use super::*;
    use mori_ledger::{DegreeRefusalDiagnostic, DegreeRefusalReason, Error};

    fn refusal(action: &str, reason: DegreeRefusalReason) -> Error {
        let (discovered_degree, caller_ceiling, pinned_supported) = match reason {
            DegreeRefusalReason::CallerCeilingExceeded => (14, 13, true),
            DegreeRefusalReason::UnsupportedPinnedDegree => (20, 25, false),
            DegreeRefusalReason::CachedDegreeMismatch { .. } => (13, 13, true),
        };
        Error::new("local-deployment", "exact-degree-unavailable").with_degree_refusal(
            DegreeRefusalDiagnostic {
                action: action.into(),
                discovered_degree,
                caller_ceiling,
                pinned_supported,
                reason,
            },
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn ledger_conversion_preserves_category_and_complete_permitted_context() {
        for (reason, context) in [
            (
                DegreeRefusalReason::CallerCeilingExceeded,
                "discovered-degree=14 caller-ceiling=13 pinned-supported=true reason=caller-ceiling-exceeded",
            ),
            (
                DegreeRefusalReason::UnsupportedPinnedDegree,
                "discovered-degree=20 caller-ceiling=25 pinned-supported=false reason=unsupported-pinned-degree",
            ),
            (
                DegreeRefusalReason::CachedDegreeMismatch { cached_degree: 12 },
                "discovered-degree=13 caller-ceiling=13 pinned-supported=true reason=cached-degree-mismatch cached-degree=12",
            ),
        ] {
            let report = ledger_operation(refusal("freeze", reason));
            assert_eq!(
                report.to_string(),
                format!(
                    "mori::command: mori::ledger::local-deployment: exact-degree-unavailable; action=\"freeze\" {context}"
                )
            );
        }
        let legacy = Error::new("local-deployment", "selected-action");
        assert_eq!(
            ledger_operation(legacy.clone()).to_string(),
            operation(legacy).to_string()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn hostile_action_is_exact_in_api_and_escaped_once_in_command_report() {
        let action = "freeze\u{1b}[31m\nforged\r\"\\\u{85}\u{202e}";
        let error = refusal(action, DegreeRefusalReason::CallerCeilingExceeded);
        assert_eq!(error.degree_refusal().unwrap().action, action);
        let message = ledger_operation(error).to_string();
        assert!(
            message.contains(r#"action="freeze\u{1b}[31m\nforged\r\"\\\u{85}\u{202e}""#),
            "{message}"
        );
        assert!(message.chars().all(|c| !c.is_control()));
        assert_eq!(
            message,
            r#"mori::command: mori::ledger::local-deployment: exact-degree-unavailable; action="freeze\u{1b}[31m\nforged\r\"\\\u{85}\u{202e}" discovered-degree=14 caller-ceiling=13 pinned-supported=true reason=caller-ceiling-exceeded"#
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn quiet_shell_reports_constructed_degree_refusal_on_stderr() {
        const CHILD: &str = "MORI_DEGREE_DIAGNOSTIC_REPORT_CHILD";
        if std::env::var_os(CHILD).is_some() {
            let report = ledger_operation(refusal(
                "freeze",
                DegreeRefusalReason::CallerCeilingExceeded,
            ));
            let mut shell = crate::shell::Shell::new(
                crate::shell::Verbosity::Quiet,
                anstream::ColorChoice::Never,
            );
            shell.report(&report);
            return;
        }
        let output = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap())
            .args(["--exact", "commands::core_io::degree_diagnostic_tests::quiet_shell_reports_constructed_degree_refusal_on_stderr", "--nocapture"])
            .env(CHILD, "1").output().unwrap();
        assert!(output.status.success());
        let stderr = String::from_utf8(output.stderr).unwrap();
        for value in [
            "exact-degree-unavailable",
            "action=\"freeze\"",
            "discovered-degree=14",
            "caller-ceiling=13",
            "caller-ceiling-exceeded",
        ] {
            assert!(stderr.contains(value), "{stderr}");
        }
        assert!(!stderr.contains('\u{1b}'));
    }
}
````

````
//! The `--json` report of `mori check`.
//!
//! Spans are UTF-8 byte ranges into the checked file. This format is our own;
//! it is not the TypeScript beta's.

use mori_ast::{Ast, NodeIdx};
use mori_checker::{Checked, DeclIdx, Support};
use mori_diagnostics::{Diagnostic, MoriDiagnostic, Severity};
use mori_lexer::TokenIdx;
use serde::Serialize;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct CheckReport {
    /// `accepted` when there are no diagnostics, otherwise `rejected`.
    pub status: &'static str,
    pub file: String,
    /// SHA-256 of the file's bytes, in lowercase hex.
    pub source_hash: String,
    /// Absent when the file did not parse.
    pub agreement: Option<Named>,
    pub declarations: Vec<DeclarationReport>,
    pub actions: Vec<ActionReport>,
    pub diagnostics: Vec<DiagnosticReport>,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct Span {
    pub start: u32,
    pub end: u32,
}

impl From<mori_span::Span> for Span {
    fn from(span: mori_span::Span) -> Self {
        Self {
            start: span.start,
            end: span.end,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct Named {
    pub name: String,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct DeclarationReport {
    /// The declaring keyword, such as `asset` or `intent`.
    pub kind: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub span: Span,
    pub name_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct ActionReport {
    pub name: String,
    pub intent: String,
    /// `local_s0` when it runs locally, `specified_only` when it is only
    /// checked; absent when its intent did not check.
    pub support: Option<&'static str>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub name_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct DiagnosticReport {
    pub code: Option<String>,
    pub severity: &'static str,
    pub message: String,
    pub help: Option<String>,
    pub labels: Vec<LabelReport>,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct LabelReport {
    pub span: Span,
    pub text: Option<String>,
    pub primary: bool,
}

impl CheckReport {
    pub fn new(
        file: String,
        source: &str,
        checked: Option<&Checked<'_>>,
        diagnostics: &[MoriDiagnostic],
    ) -> Self {
        let source_hash = Sha256::digest(source.as_bytes())
            .iter()
            .map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}"))
            .collect();
        let mut report = Self {
            status: if diagnostics.is_empty() {
                "accepted"
            } else {
                "rejected"
            },
            file,
            source_hash,
            agreement: None,
            declarations: Vec::new(),
            actions: Vec::new(),
            diagnostics: diagnostics.iter().map(DiagnosticReport::new).collect(),
        };
        if let Some(checked) = checked {
            report.fill(checked);
        }
        report
    }

    fn fill(&mut self, checked: &Checked<'_>) {
        let ast = checked.ast;
        let name_token = ast.main_token(NodeIdx::ROOT);
        self.agreement = Some(Named {
            name: ast.token_text(name_token).to_owned(),
            span: token_span(ast, name_token).into(),
        });
        for index in 0..checked.declarations.len() {
            let decl = DeclIdx::new(index);
            let node = checked.declarations.node()[index];
            let keyword = ast.main_token(node);
            self.declarations.push(DeclarationReport {
                kind: ast.token_text(keyword).to_owned(),
                name: checked.name(decl).to_owned(),
                span: ast.span(node).into(),
                name_span: token_span(ast, ast.token_after(keyword, 1)).into(),
            });
        }
        for (&node, &support) in checked.actions.node().iter().zip(checked.actions.support()) {
            let keyword = ast.main_token(node);
            self.actions.push(ActionReport {
                name: ast.token_text(ast.token_after(keyword, 1)).to_owned(),
                intent: ast.token_text(ast.token_after(keyword, 3)).to_owned(),
                support: support.map(|support| match support {
                    Support::LocalS0 => "local_s0",
                    Support::SpecifiedOnly => "specified_only",
                }),
                span: ast.span(node).into(),
                name_span: token_span(ast, ast.token_after(keyword, 1)).into(),
            });
        }
    }
}

impl DiagnosticReport {
    fn new(diagnostic: &MoriDiagnostic) -> Self {
        let severity = match diagnostic.severity() {
            Some(Severity::Warning) => "warning",
            Some(Severity::Advice) => "advice",
            _ => "error",
        };
        let mut labels: Vec<LabelReport> = diagnostic
            .labels()
            .map(|labels| {
                labels
                    .map(|label| LabelReport {
                        span: Span {
                            start: to_u32(label.offset()),
                            end: to_u32(label.offset() + label.len()),
                        },
                        text: label.label().map(str::to_owned),
                        primary: label.primary(),
                    })
                    .collect()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        // Every diagnostic reports one primary location: the marked label, or
        // else the first.
        if !labels.iter().any(|label| label.primary)
            && let Some(first) = labels.first_mut()
        {
            first.primary = true;
        }
        Self {
            code: diagnostic.code().map(|code| code.to_string()),
            severity,
            message: diagnostic.to_string(),
            help: diagnostic.help().map(|help| help.to_string()),
            labels,
        }
    }
}

fn token_span(ast: &Ast<'_>, token: TokenIdx) -> mori_span::Span {
    ast.tokens.span(token, ast.source)
}

/// Sources are at most 65,536 bytes, so offsets fit in `u32`.
fn to_u32(offset: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::try_from(offset).expect("source offsets fit in u32")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::CheckReport;

    /// Checks the source and snapshots its JSON report, recording the source.
    macro_rules! assert_report_snapshot {
        ($source:literal) => {{
            let source = indoc::indoc!($source);
            let report = match mori_parser::parse(source) {
                Err(error) => CheckReport::new("test.mori".to_owned(), source, None, &[error]),
                Ok(ast) => {
                    let result = mori_checker::check(&ast);
                    CheckReport::new("test.mori".to_owned(), source, Some(&result.checked), &result.diagnostics)
                }
            };
            insta::with_settings!({
                description => format!("Code:\n\n{source}"),
                omit_expression => true,
            }, {
                insta::assert_snapshot!(serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report).unwrap());
            });
        }};
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepted_report() {
        assert_report_snapshot!(
            r#"
            profile "moriarty-beta/1";
            agreement Oracle {
              domain Preview = { id: "preview", chain: "midnight", network: "preview" };
              observation price = { id: "price", domain: Preview };
              intent read = { operation: oracle.select(observation: price) };
              action fetch uses read;
            }
            "#
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejected_report() {
        assert_report_snapshot!(
            r#"
            profile "moriarty-beta/1";
            agreement Invoice {
              const price = 10;
              const price = pirce;
            }
            "#
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn unparsable_report() {
        assert_report_snapshot!(
            r#"
            profile "moriarty-beta/1";
            agreement Invoice {
              const price = 10
            "#
        );
    }
}
````

````
//! Cargo-style status output on stderr.

use std::fmt::Display;
use std::io::{self, Stderr, Write};

use anstream::{AutoStream, ColorChoice};
use anstyle::Style;
use mori_diagnostics::Report;
use mori_diagnostics::render::{self, WIDTH};

use crate::styles;

/// Width of the right-aligned verb column, matching cargo.
const VERB_WIDTH: usize = 12;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Verbosity {
    Quiet,
    Normal,
    Verbose,
}

/// Writes status lines such as `    Checking invoice.mori` to stderr.
///
/// Command results go to stdout and never pass through the shell. Output is
/// best effort: if stderr cannot be written, there is nowhere to report it.
pub struct Shell {
    err: AutoStream<Stderr>,
    verbosity: Verbosity,
}

impl Shell {
    pub fn new(verbosity: Verbosity, color: ColorChoice) -> Self {
        Self {
            err: AutoStream::new(io::stderr(), color),
            verbosity,
        }
    }

    /// Prints a right-aligned green verb followed by a message.
    pub fn status(&mut self, verb: &str, message: impl Display) {
        if self.verbosity != Verbosity::Quiet {
            self.aligned(verb, styles::HEADER, message);
        }
    }

    /// Like [`Shell::status`], but only under `--verbose`.
    pub fn verbose_status(&mut self, verb: &str, message: impl Display) {
        if self.verbosity == Verbosity::Verbose {
            self.aligned(verb, styles::HEADER, message);
        }
    }

    #[expect(dead_code, reason = "used once a command prints notes")]
    pub fn note(&mut self, message: impl Display) {
        if self.verbosity != Verbosity::Quiet {
            self.prefixed("note", styles::HEADER, message);
        }
    }

    #[expect(dead_code, reason = "used once a command emits warnings")]
    pub fn warn(&mut self, message: impl Display) {
        if self.verbosity != Verbosity::Quiet {
            self.prefixed("warning", styles::WARN, message);
        }
    }

    /// Prints an error line. Errors are shown even under `--quiet`.
    pub fn error(&mut self, message: impl Display) {
        self.prefixed("error", styles::ERROR, message);
    }

    /// Renders an error report, wrapped to the terminal width up to 80 columns.
    /// Errors are shown even under `--quiet`.
    pub fn report(&mut self, report: &Report) {
        let width = terminal_size::terminal_size_of(io::stderr())
            .map_or(WIDTH, |(width, _)| usize::from(width.0));
        let _ = writeln!(self.err, "{}", render::render_colored(report, width));
    }

    /// Prints `hunks` as `cargo fmt --check` does, indented to line up with a
    /// diagnostic's message.
    pub fn diff(&mut self, file: &str, hunks: &[mori_fmt::Hunk]) {
        const INDENT: &str = "    ";
        for hunk in hunks {
            let _ = writeln!(self.err, "{INDENT}Diff in {file}:{}:", hunk.line);
            for (change, line) in &hunk.lines {
                let (sign, style) = match change {
                    mori_fmt::Change::Context => (' ', Style::new()),
                    mori_fmt::Change::Removed => ('-', styles::REMOVED),
                    mori_fmt::Change::Added => ('+', styles::ADDED),
                };
                let _ = writeln!(self.err, "{INDENT}{style}{sign}{line}{style:#}");
            }
        }
        let _ = writeln!(self.err);
    }

    fn aligned(&mut self, verb: &str, style: Style, message: impl Display) {
        let message = crate::display::text(&message.to_string());
        let _ = writeln!(self.err, "{style}{verb:>VERB_WIDTH$}{style:#} {message}");
    }

    fn prefixed(&mut self, label: &str, style: Style, message: impl Display) {
        let message = crate::display::text(&message.to_string());
        let _ = writeln!(self.err, "{style}{label}:{style:#} {message}");
    }
}
````

````
//! Command failures that do not point at source code.

use std::io;
use std::path::PathBuf;

use mori_diagnostics::Diagnostic;

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum CliError {
    #[error("{code}: {message}")]
    Operation { code: String, message: String },
    #[error("could not read `{}`", crate::display::text(&path.display().to_string()))]
    Read {
        path: PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: io::Error,
    },
    #[error("could not write `{}`", crate::display::text(&path.display().to_string()))]
    Write {
        path: PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: io::Error,
    },
    #[error("`{}` does not exist", crate::display::text(&path.display().to_string()))]
    NotFound { path: PathBuf },
    #[error("could not list `{}`", crate::display::text(&path.display().to_string()))]
    Walk {
        path: PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: ignore::Error,
    },
}

impl Diagnostic for CliError {}
````

````
//! Cargo's color palette, shared by clap's help output and the shell.

use anstyle::{AnsiColor, Effects, Style};
use clap::builder::Styles;

pub const HEADER: Style = AnsiColor::Green.on_default().effects(Effects::BOLD);
pub const LITERAL: Style = AnsiColor::Cyan.on_default().effects(Effects::BOLD);
pub const PLACEHOLDER: Style = AnsiColor::Cyan.on_default();
pub const ERROR: Style = AnsiColor::Red.on_default().effects(Effects::BOLD);
pub const WARN: Style = AnsiColor::Yellow.on_default().effects(Effects::BOLD);
pub const REMOVED: Style = AnsiColor::Red.on_default();
pub const ADDED: Style = AnsiColor::Green.on_default();

pub const CLAP: Styles = Styles::styled()
    .header(HEADER)
    .usage(HEADER)
    .literal(LITERAL)
    .placeholder(PLACEHOLDER)
    .error(ERROR)
    .valid(LITERAL)
    .invalid(WARN);
````

````
/// Escape data before a terminal renderer adds its trusted styles and layout.
pub fn text(value: &str) -> String {
    let mut result = String::with_capacity(value.len());
    for character in value.chars() {
        if character.is_ascii() && !character.is_control() {
            result.push(character);
        } else {
            result.extend(character.escape_default());
        }
    }
    result
}
````

````
        impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for $ty {
            fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(decoder: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
````

````
use crate::*;
use mori_lexer::{TokenIdx, TokenKind};

/// Parses the explicitly versioned core profile; beta grammar is untouched.
pub fn parse(source: &str) -> Result<Program, Error> {
    parse_profile(source, false)
}

/// Syntax-only parser; only stage::load admits the resulting source.
pub(crate) fn parse_v2(source: &str) -> Result<Program, Error> {
    parse_profile(source, true)
}

fn parse_profile(source: &str, staged: bool) -> Result<Program, Error> {
    let lexed = mori_lexer::lex(source).map_err(|e| Error::new("lex", e.to_string()))?;
    let tokens = (0..lexed.len())
        .map(|i| {
            let idx = TokenIdx::new(i);
            let span = lexed.span(idx, source);
            let raw = &source[span.start as usize..span.end as usize];
            let text = if lexed.kind(idx) == TokenKind::String {
                mori_lexer::decode_string(raw)
            } else {
                raw.to_owned()
            };
            Tok {
                text,
                kind: lexed.kind(idx),
                start: span.start,
            }
        })
        .collect();
    let mut parser = Parser {
        tokens,
        pos: 0,
        program: Program {
            language: if staged {
                crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2
            } else {
                LANGUAGE
            }
            .into(),
            semantics: if staged {
                crate::stage::SEMANTICS_2
            } else {
                SEMANTICS
            }
            .into(),
            name: String::new(),
            states: vec![],
            assets: vec![],
            expressions: vec![],
            actions: vec![],
        },
    };
    parser.expect("language")?;
    let profile = parser.string()?;
    let expected_language = if staged {
        crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2
    } else {
        LANGUAGE
    };
    if profile != expected_language {
        return Err(parser.error(
            "profile",
            format!("Expected language \"{expected_language}\"; found {profile:?}."),
        ));
    }
    parser.expect(";")?;
    parser.expect("agreement")?;
    parser.program.name = parser.word()?;
    parser.expect("{")?;
    while !parser.eat("}") {
        if parser.eat("state") {
            let name = parser.word()?;
            parser.expect(":")?;
            let ty = parser.ty()?;
            parser.expect("=")?;
            let initial = parser.literal()?;
            parser.expect(";")?;
            parser.program.states.push(StateDecl { name, ty, initial });
        } else if parser.eat("asset") {
            let name = parser.word()?;
            parser.expect("=")?;
            parser.expect("{")?;
            parser.expect("network")?;
            parser.expect(":")?;
            let network = parser.string()?;
            parser.expect(",")?;
            parser.expect("issuer")?;
            parser.expect(":")?;
            let issuer = parser.string()?;
            parser.expect(",")?;
            parser.expect("reference")?;
            parser.expect(":")?;
            let reference = parser.string()?;
            parser.expect(",")?;
            parser.expect("scale")?;
            parser.expect(":")?;
            let Value::UInt(UInt(scale)) = parser.literal()? else {
                return Err(parser.error("asset", "Asset scale must be an unsigned integer."));
            };
            let scale = u8::try_from(scale)
                .map_err(|_| parser.error("asset", "Asset scale must fit u8."))?;
            parser.eat(",");
            parser.expect("}")?;
            parser.expect(";")?;
            parser.program.assets.push(AssetDecl {
                name,
                identity: AssetId {
                    network,
                    issuer,
                    reference,
                    scale,
                },
            });
        } else if parser.eat("action") {
            let name = parser.word()?;
            parser.expect("(")?;
            let mut inputs = vec![];
            if !parser.eat(")") {
                loop {
                    let name = parser.word()?;
                    parser.expect(":")?;
                    let ty = parser.ty()?;
                    inputs.push(InputDecl { name, ty });
                    if parser.eat(")") {
                        break;
                    }
                    parser.expect(",")?;
                }
            }
            parser.expect("{")?;
            let mut statements = vec![];
            while !parser.eat("}") {
                if parser.eat("input") {
                    if !statements.is_empty() {
                        return Err(
                            parser.error("input", "Declare action inputs before statements.")
                        );
                    }
                    let name = parser.word()?;
                    parser.expect(":")?;
                    let ty = parser.ty()?;
                    parser.expect(";")?;
                    inputs.push(InputDecl { name, ty });
                    continue;
                }
                statements.push(parser.statement()?);
                if statements.len() > MAX_STATEMENTS {
                    return Err(parser.error("bound", "Action exceeds 1,024 statements."));
                }
            }
            parser.program.actions.push(Action {
                name,
                inputs,
                statements,
            });
        } else {
            return Err(parser.error("unsupported", "Expected state, asset or action declaration; loops and native calls are unsupported."));
        }
        if parser.program.states.len() + parser.program.assets.len() + parser.program.actions.len()

            return Err(parser.error("bound", "Program exceeds 256 declarations."));
        }
    }
    if parser.peek().kind != TokenKind::Eof {
        return Err(parser.error("syntax", "Unexpected content after agreement."));
    }
    if !staged {
        validate(&parser.program)?;
    }
````
