}
struct Tok {
    text: String,
    kind: TokenKind,
    start: u32,
}
struct Parser {
    tokens: Vec<Tok>,
    pos: usize,
    program: Program,
}
impl Parser {
    fn peek(&self) -> &Tok {
        &self.tokens[self.pos]
    }
    fn error(&self, code: &str, message: impl Into<String>) -> Error {
        let mut e = Error::new(code, message);
        e.offset = Some(self.peek().start);
        e
    }
    fn eat(&mut self, text: &str) -> bool {
        if self.peek().text == text && self.peek().kind != TokenKind::String {
            self.pos += 1;
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }
    fn expect(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {
        if self.eat(text) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(self.error(
                "syntax",
                format!("Expected {text:?}; found {:?}.", self.peek().text),
            ))
        }
    }
    fn word(&mut self) -> Result<String, Error> {
        if self.peek().kind.is_word() {
            let text = self.peek().text.clone();
            self.pos += 1;
            Ok(text)
        } else {
            Err(self.error("syntax", "Expected a name."))
        }
    }
    fn string(&mut self) -> Result<String, Error> {
        if self.peek().kind == TokenKind::String {
            let text = self.peek().text.clone();
            self.pos += 1;
            Ok(text)
        } else {
            Err(self.error("syntax", "Expected a quoted string."))
        }
    }
    fn ty(&mut self) -> Result<Type, Error> {
        match self.word()?.as_str() {
            "UInt" => Ok(Type::UInt),
            "Bool" => Ok(Type::Bool),
            _ => Err(self.error("type", "Supported types are UInt and Bool.")),
        }
    }
    fn literal(&mut self) -> Result<Value, Error> {
        if self.eat("true") {
            return Ok(Value::Bool(true));
        }
        if self.eat("false") {
            return Ok(Value::Bool(false));
        }
        if self.peek().kind != TokenKind::Number {
            return Err(self.error("syntax", "Expected an unsigned integer or boolean literal."));
        }
        let raw = self.peek().text.replace('_', "");
        let n = raw.parse::<u128>().map_err(|_| {
            self.error(
                "number",
                "UInt literal must fit u128; amounts use integral atomic units.",
            )
        })?;
        self.pos += 1;
        Ok(Value::UInt(UInt(n)))
    }
    fn push(&mut self, expr: Expr) -> Result<ExprId, Error> {
        if self.program.expressions.len() >= MAX_EXPRESSIONS {
            return Err(self.error("bound", "Program exceeds 8,192 expression nodes."));
        }
        let id = self.program.expressions.len() as u16;
        self.program.expressions.push(expr);
        Ok(id)
    }
    fn expr(&mut self, minimum: u8, depth: usize) -> Result<ExprId, Error> {
        if depth > 64 {
            return Err(self.error("bound", "Expression nesting exceeds 64."));
        }
        let mut lhs = if self.eat("(") {
            let e = self.expr(0, depth + 1)?;
            self.expect(")")?;
            e
        } else if self.eat("not") {
            let value = self.expr(6, depth + 1)?;
            self.push(Expr::Not { value })?
        } else if self.peek().kind == TokenKind::Number
            || self.peek().text == "true"
            || self.peek().text == "false"
        {
            let value = self.literal()?;
            self.push(Expr::Literal { value })?
        } else {
            let name = self.word()?;
            if matches!(name.as_str(), "liability_present" | "liability_amount") && self.eat("(") {
                let duty = self.string()?;
                self.expect(")")?;
                self.push(if name == "liability_present" {
                    Expr::LiabilityPresent { name: duty }
                } else {
                    Expr::LiabilityAmount { name: duty }
                })?
            } else {
                self.push(Expr::Name { name })?
            }
        };
        loop {
            // A decoded string spelling an operator is still a string token.
            if self.peek().kind == TokenKind::String {
                break;
            }
            let next = self
                .tokens
                .get(self.pos + 1)
                .filter(|t| t.kind != TokenKind::String)
                .map(|t| t.text.as_str());
            let (op, precedence, length) = match (self.peek().text.as_str(), next) {
                ("or", _) => (BinaryOp::Or, 1, 1),
                ("and", _) => (BinaryOp::And, 2, 1),
                ("=", Some("=")) => (BinaryOp::Eq, 3, 2),
                ("not", Some("=")) => (BinaryOp::Ne, 3, 2),
                ("<", Some("=")) => (BinaryOp::Le, 3, 2),
                (">", Some("=")) => (BinaryOp::Ge, 3, 2),
                ("<", _) => (BinaryOp::Lt, 3, 1),
                (">", _) => (BinaryOp::Gt, 3, 1),
                ("+", _) => (BinaryOp::Add, 4, 1),
                ("-", _) => (BinaryOp::Sub, 4, 1),
                ("*", _) => (BinaryOp::Mul, 5, 1),
                _ => break,
            };
            if precedence < minimum {
                break;
            }
            self.pos += length;
            let rhs = self.expr(precedence + 1, depth + 1)?;
            lhs = self.push(Expr::Binary { op, lhs, rhs })?;
        }
        Ok(lhs)
    }
    fn statement(&mut self) -> Result<Statement, Error> {
        let keyword = self.word()?;
        let s=match keyword.as_str() {
            "await" if self.program.language == crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2 => {
                let label = self.word()?;
                self.expect("(")?;
                let mut binders = Vec::new();
                if !self.eat(")") {
                    loop {
                        let name = self.word()?;
                        self.expect(":")?;
                        let ty = self.ty()?;
                        binders.push(InputDecl { name, ty });
                        if self.eat(")") { break; }
                        self.expect(",")?;
                    }
                }
                self.expect("when")?;
                Statement::Await { label, binders, guard: self.expr(0, 0)? }
            },
            "let"=>{let name=self.word()?;self.expect("=")?;Statement::Let{name,value:self.expr(0,0)?}},
            "next"=>{let state=self.word()?;self.expect("=")?;Statement::Next{state,value:self.expr(0,0)?}},
            "requires"=>Statement::Requires{predicate:self.expr(0,0)?},
            "ensures"=>Statement::Ensures{predicate:self.expr(0,0)?},
            "emit"=>{let name=self.string()?;self.expect("(")?;let value=self.expr(0,0)?;self.expect(")")?;Statement::Emit{name,value}},
            "transfer"|"fee"=>{self.expect("(")?;let asset=self.word()?;self.expect(",")?;let from=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let to=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let amount=self.expr(0,0)?;self.expect(")")?;if keyword=="fee"{Statement::Fee{asset,from,to,amount}}else{Statement::Transfer{asset,from,to,amount}}},
            "liability"=>{self.expect("(")?;let name=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let asset=self.word()?;self.expect(",")?;let debtor=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let creditor=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let amount=self.expr(0,0)?;self.expect(")")?;Statement::Liability{name,asset,debtor,creditor,amount}},
            "discharge"=>{self.expect("(")?;let name=self.string()?;self.expect(",")?;let amount=self.expr(0,0)?;self.expect(")")?;Statement::Discharge{name,amount}},
            _=>return Err(self.error("unsupported",format!("Unsupported statement {keyword:?}; use let, requires, ensures, next, emit, transfer, fee, liability or discharge."))),
        };
        self.expect(";")?;
        Ok(s)
    }
}

/// Read the explicit source profile for CLI routing; this does not admit a program.
pub fn language(source: &str) -> Result<&'static str, Error> {
    let lexed = mori_lexer::lex(source).map_err(|e| Error::new("lex", e.to_string()))?;
    let mut tokens = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..lexed.len() {
        let idx = TokenIdx::new(i);
        let span = lexed.span(idx, source);
        let raw = &source[span.start as usize..span.end as usize];
        let kind = lexed.kind(idx);
        tokens.push(Tok {
            text: if kind == TokenKind::String {
                mori_lexer::decode_string(raw)
            } else {
                raw.to_owned()
            },
            kind,
            start: span.start,
        });
    }
    let mut parser = Parser {
        tokens,
        pos: 0,
        program: Program {
            language: LANGUAGE.into(),
            semantics: SEMANTICS.into(),
            name: String::new(),
            states: vec![],
            assets: vec![],
            expressions: vec![],
            actions: vec![],
        },
    };
    parser.expect("language")?;
    let profile = parser.string()?;
    match profile.as_str() {
        LANGUAGE => Ok(LANGUAGE),
        crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2 => Ok(crate::stage::LANGUAGE_2),
        _ => Err(parser.error(
            "profile",
            format!("Expected language \"{LANGUAGE}\"; found {profile:?}."),
        )),
    }
}

use crate::policy::{CostPlane, Meter};
use crate::*;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

fn failure(code: &str, message: impl Into<String>) -> Error {
    Error::new(code, message)
}
pub(crate) fn identifier(name: &str) -> bool {
    let mut bytes = name.bytes();
    matches!(bytes.next(), Some(b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z'))
        && name.len() <= 64
        && bytes.all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_')
        && !matches!(
            name,
            "language"
                | "agreement"
                | "state"
                | "asset"
                | "action"
                | "input"
                | "let"
                | "next"
                | "requires"
                | "ensures"
                | "emit"
                | "transfer"
                | "fee"
                | "liability"
                | "discharge"
                | "true"
                | "false"
                | "and"
                | "or"
                | "not"
                | "UInt"
                | "Bool"
        )
}
fn names<'a>(values: impl Iterator<Item = &'a str>, kind: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
    for name in values {
        if !identifier(name) || !seen.insert(name) {
            return Err(failure(
                "duplicate",
                format!("Invalid or duplicate {kind} name {name:?}."),
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
pub(crate) fn expr_type(
    program: &Program,
    id: ExprId,
    env: &BTreeMap<String, Type>,
    depth: usize,
) -> Result<Type, Error> {
    type_cached(
        program,
        id,
        env,
        depth,
        &mut vec![None; program.expressions.len()],
    )
}
fn type_cached(
    program: &Program,
    id: ExprId,
    env: &BTreeMap<String, Type>,
    depth: usize,
    cache: &mut [Option<Type>],
) -> Result<Type, Error> {
    if depth > 64 {
        return Err(failure("bound", "Expression depth exceeds 64."));
    }
    let index = usize::from(id);
    let node = program
        .expressions
        .get(index)
        .ok_or_else(|| failure("expression", "Expression index out of bounds."))?;
    if let Some(ty) = cache[index] {
        return Ok(ty);
    }
    let result = match node {
        Expr::LiabilityPresent { .. } => Ok(Type::Bool),
        Expr::LiabilityAmount { .. } => Ok(Type::UInt),
        Expr::Literal { value } => Ok(value.ty()),
        Expr::Name { name } => env
            .get(name)
            .copied()
            .ok_or_else(|| failure("name", format!("Unknown or forward name {name:?}."))),
        Expr::Not { value } => {
            if type_cached(program, *value, env, depth + 1, cache)? != Type::Bool {
                return Err(failure("type", "not requires Bool."));
            }
            Ok(Type::Bool)
        }
        Expr::Binary { op, lhs, rhs } => {
            let a = type_cached(program, *lhs, env, depth + 1, cache)?;
            let b = type_cached(program, *rhs, env, depth + 1, cache)?;
            let expected = match op {
                BinaryOp::And | BinaryOp::Or => Type::Bool,
                _ => Type::UInt,
            };
            if a != b || (!matches!(op, BinaryOp::Eq | BinaryOp::Ne) && a != expected) {
                return Err(failure("type", "Binary operands have incompatible types."));
            }
            Ok(
                if matches!(op, BinaryOp::Add | BinaryOp::Sub | BinaryOp::Mul) {
                    Type::UInt
                } else {
                    Type::Bool
                },
            )
        }
    }?;
    cache[index] = Some(result);
    Ok(result)
}
/// Validates even manually constructed/deserialized IR before interpretation.
pub fn validate(program: &Program) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if program.language != LANGUAGE || program.semantics != SEMANTICS {
        return Err(failure(
            "profile",
            "Unsupported language or semantics identity.",
        ));
    }
    if !identifier(&program.name) {
        return Err(failure(
            "name",
            "Agreement name must be a non-reserved ASCII identifier of at most 64 bytes.",
        ));
    }
    if program.actions.is_empty() {
        return Err(failure("program", "Program needs at least one action."));
    }

            "bound",
            "Program exceeds finite declaration/expression bounds.",
        ));
    }

            .states
            .iter()

    )?;

    let mut identities = BTreeSet::new();
    for asset in &program.assets {
        let id = &asset.identity;
        if id.network.is_empty()
            || id.issuer.is_empty()
            || id.reference.is_empty()
            || id.network.len() > 1024
            || id.issuer.len() > 1024
            || id.reference.len() > 1024
            || id.scale > 38
            || !identities.insert(id)
        {
            return Err(failure(
                "asset",
                "Asset identities must be complete, unique and use scale 0..38.",
            ));
        }
        if program.assets.iter().any(|other| {
            other.identity.network == id.network
                && other.identity.issuer == id.issuer
                && other.identity.reference == id.reference
                && other.identity.scale != id.scale
        }) {
            return Err(failure(
                "asset",
                "Same asset identity cannot have conflicting scales.",
            ));
        }
    }
    let mut depths = Vec::with_capacity(program.expressions.len());
    for (i, e) in program.expressions.iter().enumerate() {
        let refs = match e {
            Expr::Binary { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![*lhs, *rhs],
            Expr::Not { value } => vec![*value],
            _ => vec![],
        };
        let mut depth = 0;
        for r in refs {
            if usize::from(r) >= i {
                return Err(failure(
                    "expression",
                    "Expression references must point to earlier nodes; cycles are forbidden.",
                ));
            }
            depth = depth.max(depths[usize::from(r)] + 1);
        }
        if depth > 64 {
            return Err(failure("bound", "Expression depth exceeds 64."));
        }
        depths.push(depth);
    }
    let state_types: BTreeMap<_, _> = program
        .states
        .iter()
        .map(|s| (s.name.clone(), s.ty))
        .collect();
    for state in &program.states {
        if state.initial.ty() != state.ty {
            return Err(failure(
                "type",
                format!("Initial state {:?} has wrong type.", state.name),
            ));
        }
    }
    for action in &program.actions {
        if action.inputs.len() > MAX_DECLARATIONS || action.statements.len() > MAX_STATEMENTS {
            return Err(failure(
                "bound",
                "Action exceeds input or statement bounds.",
            ));
        }
        names(action.inputs.iter().map(|i| i.name.as_str()), "input")?;
        let mut env = state_types.clone();
        for input in &action.inputs {
            if env.insert(input.name.clone(), input.ty).is_some()
                || program.assets.iter().any(|a| a.name == input.name)
            {
                return Err(failure("duplicate", "Input cannot shadow a declaration."));
            }
        }
        for statement in &action.statements {
            match statement {
                // Same identity as `stage::require_core1`; only an in-memory
                // program can carry Await here, since `/1` JSON cannot.
                Statement::Await { .. } => {
                    return Err(failure("profile", "Await requires moriarty-core/2."));
                }
                Statement::Let { name, value } => {
                    let ty = expr_type(program, *value, &env, 0)?;
                    if !identifier(name)
                        || env.insert(name.clone(), ty).is_some()
                        || program.assets.iter().any(|a| a.name == *name)
                    {
                        return Err(failure("duplicate", "let cannot shadow an existing name."));
                    }
                }
                Statement::Requires { predicate } | Statement::Ensures { predicate } => {
                    if expr_type(program, *predicate, &env, 0)? != Type::Bool {
                        return Err(failure("type", "Predicate must have type Bool."));
                    }
                }
                Statement::Next { state, value } => {
                    let expected = state_types
                        .get(state)
                        .ok_or_else(|| failure("name", format!("Unknown state {state:?}.")))?;
                    if expr_type(program, *value, &env, 0)? != *expected {

                    }
                }
                Statement::Emit { name, value } => {
                    if name.is_empty() || name.len() > 1024 {
                        return Err(failure("name", "Event name must contain 1..1024 bytes."));
                    }
                    expr_type(program, *value, &env, 0)?;
                }
                Statement::Transfer {
                    asset,
                    from,
                    to,
                    amount,
                }
                | Statement::Fee {
                    asset,
                    from,
                    to,
                    amount,
                } => {
                    validate_asset(program, asset)?;
                    if from.is_empty() || to.is_empty() || from.len() > 1024 || to.len() > 1024 {
                        return Err(failure("account", "Account identities cannot be empty."));

                    debtor,
                    creditor,

                        || creditor.is_empty()

}
// New reads require a source-fixed identity. Legacy Core external duties and
// discharge-only programs keep their existing validation rules.
pub(crate) fn validate_liability_reads(p: &Program) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let mut reads = BTreeMap::new();
    for expr in &p.expressions {
        if let Expr::LiabilityPresent { name } | Expr::LiabilityAmount { name } = expr {
            if name.is_empty() || name.len() > 1024 {
                return Err(failure(
                    "liability",
                    "Liability read name must contain 1..1024 bytes.",
                ));
            }
            reads.insert(name.as_str(), None);
        }
    }
    for stmt in p.actions.iter().flat_map(|a| &a.statements) {
        if let Statement::Liability {
            name,
            asset,
            debtor,
            creditor,
            ..
        } = stmt
            && let Some(found) = reads.get_mut(name.as_str())
        {
            let identity = (
                validate_asset(p, asset)?,
                debtor.as_str(),
                creditor.as_str(),
            );
            if found.is_some_and(|previous| previous != identity) {
                return Err(failure(
                    "liability",
                    format!("Conflicting source liability identity for {name:?}."),
                ));
            }
            *found = Some(identity);
        }
    }
    for (name, identity) in reads {
        if identity.is_none() {
            return Err(failure(
                "liability",
                format!("Liability read {name:?} has no source-derived identity."),
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(crate) fn require_uint(
    p: &Program,
    id: ExprId,
    env: &BTreeMap<String, Type>,
) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if expr_type(p, id, env, 0)? != Type::UInt {
        Err(failure(
            "type",
            "Financial amount requires UInt atomic units.",
        ))
    } else {
        Ok(())
    }
}
pub(crate) fn validate_asset<'a>(p: &'a Program, name: &str) -> Result<&'a AssetId, Error> {
    p.assets
        .iter()
        .find(|a| a.name == name)
        .map(|a| &a.identity)
        .ok_or_else(|| failure("asset", format!("Unknown asset {name:?}.")))
}

fn evaluate(
    p: &Program,
    id: ExprId,
    env: &BTreeMap<String, Value>,
    snapshot: &Snapshot,
    meter: &mut Option<&mut Meter>,
) -> Result<Value, Error> {
    eval_cached(
        p,
        id,
        env,
        snapshot,
        &mut vec![None; p.expressions.len()],
        meter,
    )
}
fn charge_logical(meter: &mut Option<&mut Meter>) -> Result<(), Error> {
    if let Some(meter) = meter.as_deref_mut() {
        meter.charge(CostPlane::Logical, UInt(1))?;
    }
    Ok(())
}
fn eval_cached(
    p: &Program,
    id: ExprId,
    env: &BTreeMap<String, Value>,
    snapshot: &Snapshot,
    cache: &mut [Option<Value>],
    meter: &mut Option<&mut Meter>,
) -> Result<Value, Error> {
    let i = usize::from(id);
    if let Some(value) = &cache[i] {
        return Ok(value.clone());
    }
    // Charge the attempted node before its children or operation. Cache hits
    // above remain free, and evaluate creates a new cache for each statement.
    charge_logical(meter)?;
    let result = match &p.expressions[i] {
        Expr::LiabilityPresent { name } | Expr::LiabilityAmount { name } => {
            let row = snapshot
                .liabilities
                .binary_search_by(|l| l.name.as_str().cmp(name.as_str()))
                .ok()
                .map(|index| &snapshot.liabilities[index]);
            if matches!(&p.expressions[i], Expr::LiabilityPresent { .. }) {
                Value::Bool(row.is_some())
            } else {
                Value::UInt(row.map_or(UInt(0), |l| l.amount))
            }
        }
        Expr::Literal { value } => value.clone(),
        Expr::Name { name } => env
            .get(name)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| failure("name", format!("Unknown name {name:?}.")))?,
        Expr::Not { value } => match eval_cached(p, *value, env, snapshot, cache, meter)? {
            Value::Bool(b) => Value::Bool(!b),
            _ => return Err(failure("type", "not expects Bool.")),
        },
        Expr::Binary { op, lhs, rhs } => {
            let a = eval_cached(p, *lhs, env, snapshot, cache, meter)?;
            let b = eval_cached(p, *rhs, env, snapshot, cache, meter)?;
            match (op, a, b) {
                (BinaryOp::Add, Value::UInt(UInt(a)), Value::UInt(UInt(b))) => {
                    Value::UInt(UInt(a.checked_add(b).ok_or_else(|| {
                        failure("overflow", "UInt addition exceeds u128.")
                    })?))
                }
                (BinaryOp::Sub, Value::UInt(UInt(a)), Value::UInt(UInt(b))) => {
                    Value::UInt(UInt(a.checked_sub(b).ok_or_else(|| {
                        failure("underflow", "UInt subtraction is negative.")
                    })?))
                }
                (BinaryOp::Mul, Value::UInt(UInt(a)), Value::UInt(UInt(b))) => {
                    Value::UInt(UInt(a.checked_mul(b).ok_or_else(|| {
                        failure("overflow", "UInt multiplication exceeds u128.")
                    })?))
                }
                (BinaryOp::Eq, a, b) => Value::Bool(a == b),
                (BinaryOp::Ne, a, b) => Value::Bool(a != b),
                (BinaryOp::Lt, Value::UInt(a), Value::UInt(b)) => Value::Bool(a < b),
                (BinaryOp::Le, Value::UInt(a), Value::UInt(b)) => Value::Bool(a <= b),
                (BinaryOp::Gt, Value::UInt(a), Value::UInt(b)) => Value::Bool(a > b),
                (BinaryOp::Ge, Value::UInt(a), Value::UInt(b)) => Value::Bool(a >= b),
                (BinaryOp::And, Value::Bool(a), Value::Bool(b)) => Value::Bool(a && b),
                (BinaryOp::Or, Value::Bool(a), Value::Bool(b)) => Value::Bool(a || b),
                _ => return Err(failure("type", "Invalid operand types.")),
            }
        }
    };
    cache[i] = Some(result.clone());
    Ok(result)
}
fn amount(
    p: &Program,
    id: ExprId,
    env: &BTreeMap<String, Value>,
    snapshot: &Snapshot,
    meter: &mut Option<&mut Meter>,
) -> Result<UInt, Error> {
    match evaluate(p, id, env, snapshot, meter)? {
        Value::UInt(v) => Ok(v),
        _ => Err(failure("type", "Expected UInt amount.")),
    }
}
// Core also supports incoming duties without a source declaration. Only names

fn liability_identities(p: &Program) -> Result<BTreeMap<&str, (&AssetId, &str, &str)>, Error> {

                return Err(failure(
                    "liability",
                    format!("Conflicting source liability identity for {name:?}."),
                ));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(identities)
}
pub(crate) fn scenario_snapshot(p: &Program, a: &Action, s: &Scenario) -> Result<Snapshot, Error> {
    if s.balances.len() > 4096 || s.liabilities.len() > 1024 {
        return Err(failure(
            "bound",
            "Scenario exceeds 4,096 balances or 1,024 liabilities.",
        ));
    }
    let added_liabilities = a
        .statements
        .iter()
        .filter(|stmt| matches!(stmt, Statement::Liability { .. }))
        .count();
    let trace_records =
        p.states.len() + s.balances.len() + s.liabilities.len() + added_liabilities + 1;
    if trace_records.saturating_mul(a.statements.len() + 2) > MAX_TRACE_CELLS {
        return Err(failure(
            "bound",
            "Scenario and action exceed 65,536 trace snapshot records.",
        ));
    }
    if !s.state.is_empty() && s.state.len() != p.states.len() {
        return Err(failure(
            "state",
            "Provide either initial state {} or every declared state value.",
        ));
    }
    let mut state = BTreeMap::new();
    for d in &p.states {
        let value = if s.state.is_empty() {
            d.initial.clone()
        } else {
            s.state
                .get(&d.name)
                .ok_or_else(|| failure("state", format!("Missing state {:?}.", d.name)))?
                .clone()
        };
        if value.ty() != d.ty {
            return Err(failure(
                "state",
                format!("Wrong type for state {:?}.", d.name),
            ));
        }
        state.insert(d.name.clone(), value);
    }
    if s.inputs.len() != a.inputs.len() {
        return Err(failure(
            "input",
            "Scenario must provide exactly the selected action's inputs.",
        ));
    }
    for input in &a.inputs {
        if s.inputs.get(&input.name).map(Value::ty) != Some(input.ty) {
            return Err(failure(
                "input",
                format!("Missing or wrong type for input {:?}.", input.name),
            ));
        }
    }
    let ids: BTreeSet<_> = p.assets.iter().map(|a| a.identity.clone()).collect();
    let mut keys = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut balances = s.balances.clone();
    for b in &balances {
        if !ids.contains(&b.asset) {
            return Err(failure(
                "asset",
                format!(
                    "Undeclared exact asset identity for account {:?}.",
                    b.account
                ),
            ));
        }
        if b.account.is_empty()
            || b.account.len() > 1024
            || !keys.insert((b.asset.clone(), b.account.clone()))
        {
            return Err(failure(
                "balance",
                "Duplicate or invalid balance account/asset.",
            ));
        }
    }
    for stmt in &a.statements {
        if let Statement::Transfer {
            asset, from, to, ..
        }
        | Statement::Fee {
            asset, from, to, ..
        } = stmt
        {
            let id = validate_asset(p, asset)?;
            for account in [from, to] {
                if !keys.contains(&(id.clone(), account.clone())) {
                    return Err(failure(
                        "balance",
                        format!("Missing explicit balance for {account:?} and asset {asset:?}."),
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    balances.sort_by(|a, b| (&a.asset, &a.account).cmp(&(&b.asset, &b.account)));
    let identities = liability_identities(p)?;
    let mut liabilities = s.liabilities.clone();
    let mut names = BTreeSet::new();
    for l in &liabilities {
        if !ids.contains(&l.asset) {
            return Err(failure(
                "asset",
                "Liability uses undeclared exact asset identity.",
            ));
        }
        if l.name.is_empty()
            || l.name.len() > 1024
            || l.debtor.is_empty()
            || l.creditor.is_empty()
            || l.debtor.len() > 1024
            || l.creditor.len() > 1024
            || !names.insert(l.name.clone())
        {
            return Err(failure(
                "liability",
                "Invalid or duplicate liability identity.",
            ));
        }
        if let Some(identity) = identities.get(l.name.as_str())
            && *identity != (&l.asset, l.debtor.as_str(), l.creditor.as_str())
        {
            return Err(failure(
                "liability",
                format!("Existing liability identity differs for {:?}.", l.name),
            ));
        }
    }
    liabilities.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
    Ok(Snapshot {
        state,
        balances,
        liabilities,
    })
}
fn move_funds(
    snapshot: &mut Snapshot,
    id: &AssetId,
    from: &str,
    to: &str,
    amount: UInt,
) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let f = snapshot
        .balances
        .iter()
        .position(|b| b.asset == *id && b.account == from)
        .ok_or_else(|| failure("balance", "Missing source balance."))?;
    let t = snapshot
        .balances
        .iter()
        .position(|b| b.asset == *id && b.account == to)
        .ok_or_else(|| failure("balance", "Missing recipient balance."))?;
    let debit = snapshot.balances[f]
        .amount
        .0
        .checked_sub(amount.0)
        .ok_or_else(|| failure("balance", format!("Insufficient balance for {from:?}.")))?;
    if f != t {
        let credit = snapshot.balances[t]
            .amount
            .0
            .checked_add(amount.0)
            .ok_or_else(|| failure("overflow", "Recipient balance exceeds u128."))?;
        snapshot.balances[f].amount = UInt(debit);
        snapshot.balances[t].amount = UInt(credit);
    }
    Ok(())
}
/// Shared scalar statement execution for legacy actions and admitted segments.
fn execute_statement(
    program: &Program,
    stmt: &Statement,
    env: &mut BTreeMap<String, Value>,
    current: &mut Snapshot,
    meter: &mut Option<&mut Meter>,
    effects: &mut Vec<Effect>,
) -> Result<Option<Value>, Error> {
    charge_logical(meter)?;
    match stmt {
        Statement::Await { guard, .. } => {
            let v = evaluate(program, *guard, env, current, meter)?;
            Ok(Some(v))
        }
        Statement::Let { name, value } => {
            let v = evaluate(program, *value, env, current, meter)?;
            env.insert(name.clone(), v.clone());
            Ok(Some(v))
        }
        Statement::Requires { predicate } | Statement::Ensures { predicate } => {
            let v = evaluate(program, *predicate, env, current, meter)?;
            if v != Value::Bool(true) {
                return Err(failure(
                    if matches!(stmt, Statement::Requires { .. }) {
                        "requires"
                    } else {
                        "ensures"
                    },
                    "Action predicate evaluated to false.",
                ));
            }
            Ok(Some(v))
        }
        Statement::Next { state, value } => {
            let after = evaluate(program, *value, env, current, meter)?;
            let before = current.state[state].clone();
            current.state.insert(state.clone(), after.clone());
            env.insert(state.clone(), after.clone());
            effects.push(Effect::State {
                name: state.clone(),
                before,
                after: after.clone(),
            });
            Ok(Some(after))
        }
        Statement::Emit { name, value } => {
            let v = evaluate(program, *value, env, current, meter)?;
            effects.push(Effect::Emit {
                name: name.clone(),
                value: v.clone(),
            });
            Ok(Some(v))
        }
        Statement::Transfer {
            asset,
            from,
            to,
            amount: expr,
        }
        | Statement::Fee {
            asset,
            from,
            to,
            amount: expr,
        } => {
            let amount = amount(program, *expr, env, current, meter)?;
            let id = validate_asset(program, asset)?.clone();
            move_funds(current, &id, from, to, amount)?;
            effects.push(if matches!(stmt, Statement::Fee { .. }) {
                Effect::Fee {
                    asset: id,
                    from: from.clone(),
                    to: to.clone(),
                    amount,
                }
            } else {
                Effect::Transfer {
                    asset: id,
                    from: from.clone(),
                    to: to.clone(),
                    amount,
                }
            });
            Ok(Some(Value::UInt(amount)))
        }
        Statement::Liability {
            name,
            asset,
            debtor,
            creditor,
            amount: expr,
        } => {
            let amount = amount(program, *expr, env, current, meter)?;
            let id = validate_asset(program, asset)?.clone();
            let found = current.liabilities.iter().position(|l| l.name == *name);
            let before = if let Some(index) = found {
                let l = &current.liabilities[index];
                if l.asset != id || l.debtor != *debtor || l.creditor != *creditor {
                    return Err(failure("liability", "Existing liability identity differs."));
                }
                l.amount
            } else {
                UInt(0)
            };
            let after = UInt(
                before
                    .0
                    .checked_add(amount.0)
                    .ok_or_else(|| failure("overflow", "Liability exceeds u128."))?,
            );
            if let Some(index) = found {
                current.liabilities[index].amount = after;
            } else {
                current.liabilities.push(Liability {
                    name: name.clone(),
                    asset: id.clone(),
                    debtor: debtor.clone(),
                    creditor: creditor.clone(),
                    amount: after,
                });
                current.liabilities.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
            }
            effects.push(Effect::Liability {
                name: name.clone(),
                asset: id,
                debtor: debtor.clone(),
                creditor: creditor.clone(),
                before,
                after,
            });
            Ok(Some(Value::UInt(amount)))
        }
        Statement::Discharge { name, amount: expr } => {
            let amount = amount(program, *expr, env, current, meter)?;
            let l = current
                .liabilities
                .iter_mut()
                .find(|l| l.name == *name)
                .ok_or_else(|| {
                    failure("liability", format!("Unknown residual liability {name:?}."))
                })?;
            let before = l.amount;
            let after =
                UInt(before.0.checked_sub(amount.0).ok_or_else(|| {
                    failure("liability", "Discharge exceeds residual liability.")
                })?);
            l.amount = after;
            effects.push(Effect::Liability {
                name: name.clone(),
                asset: l.asset.clone(),
                debtor: l.debtor.clone(),
                creditor: l.creditor.clone(),
                before,
                after,
            });
            Ok(Some(Value::UInt(amount)))
        }
    }
}

/// Executes one finite action on a clone. A refusal exposes no committed effects.
pub fn simulate(program: &Program, action: &str, scenario: &Scenario) -> Result<Execution, Error> {
    simulate_with_meter(program, action, scenario, None)
}
pub(crate) fn simulate_with_meter(
    program: &Program,
    action: &str,
    scenario: &Scenario,
    mut meter: Option<&mut Meter>,
) -> Result<Execution, Error> {
    validate(program)?;
    let selected = program
        .actions
        .iter()
        .find(|a| a.name == action)
        .ok_or_else(|| failure("action", format!("Unknown action {action:?}.")))?;
    let pre = scenario_snapshot(program, selected, scenario)?;
    let mut current = pre.clone();
    let mut env = current.state.clone();
    env.extend(scenario.inputs.clone());
    let mut steps = vec![];
    let mut all_effects = vec![];
    for (i, stmt) in selected.statements.iter().enumerate() {
        let mut effects = vec![];
        let result = execute_statement(
            program,
            stmt,
            &mut env,
            &mut current,
            &mut meter,
            &mut effects,
        );
        let value = result.map_err(|mut e| {
            e.step = Some(i as u16);
            e
        })?;
        all_effects.extend(effects.clone());
        steps.push(Step {
            index: i as u16,
            statement: stmt.clone(),
            value,
            snapshot: current.clone(),
            effects,
        });
    }
    Ok(Execution {
        semantics: SEMANTICS.into(),
        action: action.into(),
        pre,
        post: current,
        steps,
        effects: all_effects,
    })
}
/// Environment seed supplied only by stage admission.
pub enum SegmentEntry<'a> {
    Start {
        inputs: &'a [crate::stage::NamedValue],
    },
    Resume {
        site: u16,
        captures: &'a [crate::stage::NamedValue],
        event: &'a [crate::stage::NamedValue],
    },
}

pub enum SegmentRun {
    NotAdvanced,
    Ran {
        execution: Box<Execution>,
        exit_site: u16,
        captures_out: Vec<crate::stage::NamedValue>,
    },
}

/// Runs an already-admitted finite source segment with the same scalar executor
/// as legacy simulation. The caller owns admission, publication and work policy.
pub(crate) fn run_segment(
    sp: &crate::stage::StagedProgram,
    action: usize,
    entry: SegmentEntry<'_>,
    boundary: Snapshot,
    meter: &mut Meter,
) -> Result<SegmentRun, Error> {
    let program = sp.program();
    let selected = &program.actions[action];
    let plan = &sp.plan().actions[action];
    let pre = boundary;
    let mut current = pre.clone();
    let mut env = pre.state.clone();
    let mut meter = Some(meter);
    let mut steps = Vec::new();
    let mut all_effects = Vec::new();
    let begin = match entry {
        SegmentEntry::Start { inputs } => {
            env.extend(inputs.iter().map(|v| (v.name.clone(), v.value.clone())));
            0
        }
        SegmentEntry::Resume {
            site,
            captures,
            event,
        } => {
            env.extend(
                captures
                    .iter()
                    .chain(event)
                    .map(|v| (v.name.clone(), v.value.clone())),
            );
            let ordinal = usize::from(plan.sites[usize::from(site) - 1].ordinal);
            let statement = &selected.statements[ordinal];
            let mut effects = Vec::new();
            // execute_statement charges dispatch once, then visits the guard.
            let value = execute_statement(
                program,
                statement,
                &mut env,
                &mut current,
                &mut meter,
                &mut effects,
            )
            .map_err(|mut error| {
                error.step = Some(ordinal as u16);
                error
            })?;
            if value != Some(Value::Bool(true)) {
                return Ok(SegmentRun::NotAdvanced);
            }
            steps.push(Step {
                index: ordinal as u16,
                statement: statement.clone(),
                value,
                snapshot: pre.clone(),
                effects,
            });
            ordinal + 1
        }
    };
    let mut exit_site = 0;
    let mut captures_out = Vec::new();
    for (ordinal, statement) in selected.statements.iter().enumerate().skip(begin) {
        if matches!(statement, Statement::Await { .. }) {
            // Entry charge is attempted now; guard and its Step belong to resume.
            charge_logical(&mut meter).map_err(|mut error| {
                error.step = Some(ordinal as u16);
                error
            })?;
            let site = plan
                .sites
                .iter()
                .find(|s| usize::from(s.ordinal) == ordinal)
                .ok_or_else(|| failure("stage_site", "Await site is absent from stage plan."))?;
            exit_site = site.site;
            for slot in &site.captures {
                let value = env
                    .get(&slot.name)
                    .cloned()
                    .ok_or_else(|| failure("name", format!("Unknown name {:?}.", slot.name)))?;
                captures_out.push(crate::stage::NamedValue {
                    name: slot.name.clone(),
                    value,
                });
            }
            break;
        }
        let mut effects = Vec::new();
        let value = execute_statement(
            program,
            statement,
            &mut env,
            &mut current,
            &mut meter,
            &mut effects,
        )
        .map_err(|mut error| {
            error.step = Some(ordinal as u16);
            error
        })?;
        all_effects.extend(effects.clone());
        steps.push(Step {
            index: ordinal as u16,
            statement: statement.clone(),
            value,
            snapshot: current.clone(),
            effects,
        });
    }
    Ok(SegmentRun::Ran {
        execution: Box::new(Execution {
            semantics: program.semantics.clone(),
            action: selected.name.clone(),
            pre,
            post: current,
            steps,
            effects: all_effects,
        }),
        exit_site,
        captures_out,
    })
}

/// Recomputes all steps and rejects at the first deterministic divergence.
pub fn replay(
    program: &Program,
    action: &str,
    scenario: &Scenario,
    expected: &Execution,
) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let actual = simulate(program, action, scenario)?;
    if actual.semantics != expected.semantics
        || actual.action != expected.action
        || actual.pre != expected.pre
    {
        return Err(failure(
            "replay",
            "Execution identity or predecessor differs.",
        ));
    }
    for i in 0..actual.steps.len().max(expected.steps.len()) {
        if actual.steps.get(i) != expected.steps.get(i) {
            let mut e = failure("replay", format!("First divergence at step {i}."));
            e.step = Some(i as u16);
            return Err(e);
        }
    }
    if actual.effects != expected.effects || actual.post != expected.post {
        return Err(failure(
            "replay",
            "Complete effect sequence or poststate differs.",
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

//! Local primitive interpretation cost, separate from execution and replay schemas.
//! Dust, service and external costs are unmeasured by this profile.
use crate::policy::{Cost, Meter};
use crate::{DetailedReplayError, Error, Execution, Program, Scenario, UInt, compare_execution};
use serde::Serialize;

pub const LOGICAL_COST_PROFILE: &str = "moriarty-reference-logical-cost/1";
pub const LOGICAL_COST_PROFILE_2: &str = "moriarty-reference-logical-cost/2";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CostReport {
    pub profile: String,
    pub cap: UInt,
    pub used: UInt,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MeteredExecution {
    pub execution: Execution,
    pub cost: CostReport,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
#[error("{error}")]
pub struct MeteredExecutionError {
    pub error: Error,
    pub cost: CostReport,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
#[error("{error}")]
pub struct MeteredReplayError {
    pub error: DetailedReplayError,
    pub cost: CostReport,
}
/// Executes with a separately trusted, unsigned local logical-work cap.
/// A refusal reports charged attempts and exposes no partial execution.
// The refusal carries its charged cost report by design.
#[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
pub fn simulate_metered(
    program: &Program,
    action: &str,
    scenario: &Scenario,
    cap: UInt,
) -> Result<MeteredExecution, MeteredExecutionError> {
    let mut meter = Meter::new(Cost {
        logical: cap,
        ..Cost::default()
    });
    let result = crate::runtime::simulate_with_meter(program, action, scenario, Some(&mut meter));
    let cost = CostReport {
        profile: LOGICAL_COST_PROFILE.into(),
        cap,
        used: meter.used().logical,
    };
    match result {
        Ok(execution) => Ok(MeteredExecution { execution, cost }),
        Err(error) => Err(MeteredExecutionError { error, cost }),
    }
}
/// Reconstructs once under the trusted cap, then uses existing first-divergence
/// comparison. Comparison and serialization work are outside this cost profile.
// The refusal carries its charged cost report by design.
#[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
pub fn replay_detailed_metered(
    program: &Program,
    action: &str,
    scenario: &Scenario,
    candidate: &Execution,
    cap: UInt,
) -> Result<CostReport, MeteredReplayError> {
    let metered =
        simulate_metered(program, action, scenario, cap).map_err(|refused| MeteredReplayError {
            error: DetailedReplayError::Execution(refused.error),
            cost: refused.cost,
        })?;
    compare_execution(&metered.execution, candidate).map_err(|difference| MeteredReplayError {
        error: DetailedReplayError::Divergence(difference),
        cost: metered.cost.clone(),
    })?;
    Ok(metered.cost)
}

//! Bounded JSON parsing that rejects duplicate keys before schema decoding.
use crate::Error;
use serde::de::{DeserializeSeed, MapAccess, SeqAccess, Visitor};
use serde_json::{Map, Value};
use std::{cell::Cell, fmt};
const MAX_BYTES: usize = 1_048_576;
struct Seed<'a> {
    depth: usize,
    nodes: &'a Cell<usize>,
}
impl<'de> DeserializeSeed<'de> for Seed<'_> {
    type Value = Value;
    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(self, d: D) -> Result<Value, D::Error> {
        use serde::de::Error as _;
        self.nodes.set(self.nodes.get() + 1);
        if self.depth > 32 || self.nodes.get() > 65_536 {
            return Err(D::Error::custom("JSON work/depth limit"));
        }
        d.deserialize_any(self)
    }
}
impl<'de> Visitor<'de> for Seed<'_> {
    type Value = Value;
    fn expecting(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("bounded JSON")
    }
    fn visit_bool<E: serde::de::Error>(self, v: bool) -> Result<Value, E> {
        Ok(Value::Bool(v))
    }
    fn visit_unit<E: serde::de::Error>(self) -> Result<Value, E> {
        Ok(Value::Null)
    }
    fn visit_i64<E: serde::de::Error>(self, v: i64) -> Result<Value, E> {
        Ok(v.into())
    }
    fn visit_u64<E: serde::de::Error>(self, v: u64) -> Result<Value, E> {
        Ok(v.into())
    }
    fn visit_f64<E: serde::de::Error>(self, v: f64) -> Result<Value, E> {
        serde_json::Number::from_f64(v)
            .map(Value::Number)
            .ok_or_else(|| E::custom("nonfinite JSON number"))
    }
    fn visit_str<E: serde::de::Error>(self, v: &str) -> Result<Value, E> {
        Ok(v.into())
    }
    fn visit_string<E: serde::de::Error>(self, v: String) -> Result<Value, E> {
        Ok(v.into())
    }
    fn visit_seq<A: SeqAccess<'de>>(self, mut a: A) -> Result<Value, A::Error> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        while let Some(v) = a.next_element_seed(Seed {
            depth: self.depth + 1,
            nodes: self.nodes,
        })? {
            out.push(v)
        }
        Ok(Value::Array(out))
    }
    fn visit_map<A: MapAccess<'de>>(self, mut a: A) -> Result<Value, A::Error> {
        use serde::de::Error as _;
        let mut out = Map::new();
        while let Some(k) = a.next_key::<String>()? {
            if out.contains_key(&k) {
                return Err(A::Error::custom("duplicate decoded key"));
            }
            let v = a.next_value_seed(Seed {
                depth: self.depth + 1,
                nodes: self.nodes,
            })?;
            out.insert(k, v);
        }
        Ok(Value::Object(out))
    }
}
/// Strict recursive JSON value decoding for versioned DTO dynamic fields.
/// Duplicate decoded keys and the existing depth/node bounds apply even when
/// a consumer invokes serde directly instead of the bounded text entry point.
pub fn deserialize_strict<'de, D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(decoder: D) -> Result<Value, D::Error> {
    let nodes = Cell::new(0);
    Seed {
        depth: 0,
        nodes: &nodes,
    }
    .deserialize(decoder)
}
pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Value, Error> {
    parse_inner(text, MAX_BYTES, "JSON exceeds 1 MiB")
}
/// The same strict parser under a caller-selected byte ceiling. Duplicate-key,
/// depth (32) and node (65,536) limits are unchanged; `/2` stage files use it.
pub fn parse_limited(text: &str, max: usize, too_large: &'static str) -> Result<Value, Error> {
    parse_inner(text, max, too_large)
}
fn parse_inner(text: &str, max: usize, too_large: &'static str) -> Result<Value, Error> {
    use serde::de::DeserializeSeed;
    if text.len() > max {
        return Err(Error::new("json", too_large));
    }
    let nodes = Cell::new(0);
    let mut decoder = serde_json::Deserializer::from_str(text);
    let value = Seed {
        depth: 0,
        nodes: &nodes,
    }
    .deserialize(&mut decoder)
    .map_err(|e| Error::new("json", e.to_string()))?;
    decoder
        .end()
        .map_err(|e| Error::new("json", e.to_string()))?;
    Ok(value)
}

/// ASCII-safe pretty JSON that fits the same public reader profile, including
/// the final newline added by CLI printing. Parsed values and signing bytes
/// are preserved; terminal-controlled Unicode remains visibly escaped.
pub fn export(value: &impl serde::Serialize) -> Result<String, Error> {
    let json =
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(value).map_err(|e| Error::new("json", e.to_string()))?;
    parse(&json)?;
    let mut display = String::with_capacity(json.len());
    for character in json.chars() {
        if character.is_ascii() && (!character.is_control() || character == '\n') {
            display.push(character);
        } else {
            for unit in character.encode_utf16(&mut [0; 2]) {
                use std::fmt::Write;
                write!(&mut display, "\\u{unit:04x}").expect("writing to String cannot fail");
            }
        }
        if display.len() >= MAX_BYTES {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "json",
                "Escaped JSON and final newline exceed 1 MiB",
            ));
        }
    }
    parse(&display)?;
    Ok(display)
}
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn duplicate_decoded_keys_and_trailing_data_reject() {
        assert!(parse(r#"{"x":1,"\u0078":2}"#).is_err());
        assert!(parse("{} []").is_err());
        assert!(parse(r#"{"x":"1"}"#).is_ok());
    }
}

//! Deterministic cost accounting and scoped local authority.
//! Authentication of grants and settlement observations belongs to the caller.
use crate::{Error, UInt};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Cost {
    pub logical: UInt,
    pub dust: UInt,
    pub service: UInt,
    pub external: UInt,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CostPlane {
    Logical,
    Dust,
    Service,
    External,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Meter {
    caps: Cost,
    used: Cost,
}
impl Meter {
    pub fn new(caps: Cost) -> Self {
        Self {
            caps,
            used: Cost::default(),
        }
    }
    pub fn used(&self) -> Cost {
        self.used
    }
    pub fn charge(&mut self, plane: CostPlane, amount: UInt) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let (used, cap) = match plane {
            CostPlane::Logical => (&mut self.used.logical, self.caps.logical),
            CostPlane::Dust => (&mut self.used.dust, self.caps.dust),
            CostPlane::Service => (&mut self.used.service, self.caps.service),
            CostPlane::External => (&mut self.used.external, self.caps.external),
        };
        let next = used
            .0
            .checked_add(amount.0)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("meter", "cost counter overflow"))?;
        if next > cap.0 {
            return Err(Error::new("meter", "cost plane cap exceeded"));
        }
        *used = UInt(next);
        Ok(())
    }
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Reservation {
    Reserved(UInt),
    Unknown(UInt),
    Settled(UInt),
    Released,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FeeCapability {
    id: String,
    network: String,
    anchor: String,
    program: String,
    action: String,
    beneficiary: String,
    cap: UInt,
    spent: UInt,
    reservations: BTreeMap<String, Reservation>,
}
impl FeeCapability {
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn new(
        id: &str,
        network: &str,
        anchor: &str,
        program: &str,
        action: &str,
        beneficiary: &str,
        cap: UInt,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            id: id.into(),
            network: network.into(),
            anchor: anchor.into(),
            program: program.into(),
            action: action.into(),
            beneficiary: beneficiary.into(),
            cap,
            spent: UInt(0),
            reservations: BTreeMap::new(),
        }
    }
    pub fn spent(&self) -> UInt {
        self.spent
    }
    pub fn available(&self) -> Result<UInt, Error> {
        let pending = self
            .reservations
            .values()
            .try_fold(0_u128, |total, r| match r {
                Reservation::Reserved(a) | Reservation::Unknown(a) => total.checked_add(a.0),
                _ => Some(total),
            })
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("sponsor", "reserved capacity overflow"))?;
        self.cap
            .0
            .checked_sub(self.spent.0)
            .and_then(|n| n.checked_sub(pending))
            .map(UInt)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("sponsor", "invalid capacity accounting"))
    }
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn reserve(
        &mut self,
        id: &str,
        network: &str,
        anchor: &str,
        program: &str,
        action: &str,
        beneficiary: &str,
        amount: UInt,
    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
        if [
            &self.id,
            &self.network,
            &self.anchor,
            &self.program,
            &self.action,
            &self.beneficiary,
        ]
        .iter()
        .any(|s| s.is_empty())
            || id.is_empty()
            || (network, anchor, program, action, beneficiary)
                != (
                    self.network.as_str(),
                    self.anchor.as_str(),
                    self.program.as_str(),
                    self.action.as_str(),
                    self.beneficiary.as_str(),
                )
        {
            return Err(Error::new("sponsor", "fee capability scope mismatch"));
        }
        if self.reservations.contains_key(id) {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "sponsor",
                "reservation identity already consumed",
            ));
        }
        if amount.0 > self.available()?.0 {
            return Err(Error::new("sponsor", "insufficient sponsor capacity"));
        }
        self.reservations
            .insert(id.into(), Reservation::Reserved(amount));
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn mark_unknown(&mut self, id: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {
        match self.reservations.get_mut(id) {
            Some(r @ Reservation::Reserved(_)) => {
                let Reservation::Reserved(a) = *r else {
                    unreachable!()
                };
                *r = Reservation::Unknown(a);
                Ok(())
            }
            _ => Err(Error::new(
                "sponsor",
                "reservation is not pending submission",
            )),
        }
    }
    /// Release a reservation that has never been submitted. Timeout is insufficient.
    pub fn release_unused(&mut self, id: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {
        match self.reservations.get_mut(id) {
            Some(r @ Reservation::Reserved(_)) => {
                *r = Reservation::Released;
                Ok(())
            }
            _ => Err(Error::new(
                "sponsor",
                "cannot release an unknown or finalized spend",
            )),
        }
    }
    /// The caller must authenticate a final settlement observation before reconciling.
    pub fn settle(&mut self, id: &str, actual: UInt) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let bound = match self.reservations.get(id) {
            Some(Reservation::Reserved(a) | Reservation::Unknown(a)) => *a,
            _ => return Err(Error::new("sponsor", "reservation is absent or finalized")),
        };
        if actual.0 > bound.0 {
            return Err(Error::new(
                "sponsor",
                "settled DUST exceeds reserved authority",
            ));
        }
        let spent = self
            .spent
            .0
            .checked_add(actual.0)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("sponsor", "settled spend overflow"))?;
        if spent > self.cap.0 {
            return Err(Error::new("sponsor", "sponsor cap exceeded"));
        }
        self.spent = UInt(spent);
        self.reservations
            .insert(id.into(), Reservation::Settled(actual));
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum Role {
    Clear,
    Prove,
    Relay,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct RoleGrant {
    pub members: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub quorum: u16,
    pub calls: BTreeSet<(String, String)>,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct FederationPolicy {
    pub network: String,
    pub anchor: String,
    pub epoch: UInt,
    pub grants: BTreeMap<Role, RoleGrant>,
    pub revoked: BTreeSet<String>,
}
impl FederationPolicy {
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub fn authorize(
        &self,
        role: Role,
        members: &[String],
        epoch: UInt,
        network: &str,
        anchor: &str,
        program: &str,
        action: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
        if epoch != self.epoch
            || network != self.network
            || anchor != self.anchor
            || network.is_empty()
            || anchor.is_empty()
        {
            return Err(Error::new("policy", "policy epoch or domain mismatch"));
        }
        let grant = self
            .grants
            .get(&role)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::new("policy", "role has no grant"))?;
        let unique: BTreeSet<_> = members.iter().collect();
        if grant.quorum == 0
            || usize::from(grant.quorum) > grant.members.len()
            || unique.len() != members.len()
            || unique.len() < usize::from(grant.quorum)
            || unique
                .iter()
                .any(|m| !grant.members.contains(*m) || self.revoked.contains(*m))
            || !grant.calls.contains(&(program.into(), action.into()))
        {
            return Err(Error::new("policy", "role, quorum or call scope denied"));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

//! Lexer for `moriarty-beta/1` source.
//!
//! Turns source text into [`Tokens`] in a single pass.
//!
//! Lexing stops at the first error. Whitespace is skipped; comments are kept
//! separately for the formatter and do not count toward [`MAX_TOKENS`].

mod diagnostics;
mod number;
mod scan;
mod string;
mod token;

#[cfg(test)]
mod proptests;
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use mori_diagnostics::MoriDiagnostic;
use mori_span::Span;
use soa_rs::Soa;

use crate::number::NumberError;
use crate::string::StringErrorKind;

pub use crate::token::{Comment, Token, TokenIdx, TokenKind, Tokens};

/// Largest accepted source file, in bytes.
pub const MAX_SOURCE_BYTES: usize = 65_536;
/// Most tokens in one file, including the end-of-file token.
pub const MAX_TOKENS: usize = 8_192;
/// Longest identifier or keyword, in bytes.
pub const MAX_IDENT_BYTES: usize = 64;
/// Longest decoded string, in UTF-8 bytes.
pub const MAX_STRING_BYTES: usize = 1_024;

/// The text of a string token, with escapes decoded.
///
/// `raw` must be the full text of a [`TokenKind::String`] token, quotes
/// included, as produced by [`lex`].
pub fn decode_string(raw: &str) -> String {
    let mut text = String::with_capacity(raw.len());
    string::decode_with(raw, |c| text.push(c)).expect("lexed strings are valid");
    text
}

/// Splits `source` into tokens and comments, or reports the first error.
pub fn lex(source: &str) -> Result<Tokens, MoriDiagnostic> {
    if source.len() > MAX_SOURCE_BYTES {
        return Err(diagnostics::source_too_large(source.len()));
    }
    Lexer::new(source).run(false)
}

/// Identify a leading profile token without requiring the remaining source to
/// lex successfully. Inspect only a bounded prefix; full parsing retains all
/// source and token limits.
pub fn first_token_text(source: &str) -> Result<&str, MoriDiagnostic> {
    let end = source.floor_char_boundary(source.len().min(MAX_SOURCE_BYTES));
    let prefix = &source[..end];
    let tokens = Lexer::new(prefix).run(true)?;
    Ok(tokens.span(TokenIdx::new(0), prefix).source_text(prefix))
}

struct Lexer<'src> {
    source: &'src str,
    bytes: &'src [u8],
    pos: usize,
    tokens: Soa<Token>,
    comments: Soa<Comment>,
}

impl<'src> Lexer<'src> {
    fn new(source: &'src str) -> Self {
        Self {
            source,
            bytes: source.as_bytes(),
            pos: 0,
            // Roughly one token per eight bytes, as in Zig.
            tokens: Soa::with_capacity(source.len() / 8 + 1),
            comments: Soa::new(),
        }
    }

    fn run(mut self, first_only: bool) -> Result<Tokens, MoriDiagnostic> {
        while let Some(&b) = self.bytes.get(self.pos) {
            let start = self.pos;
            match b {
                b' ' | b'\t' | b'\r' | b'\n' => self.pos += 1,
                b'/' if self.peek(1) == Some(b'/') => self.line_comment(start),
                b'/' if self.peek(1) == Some(b'*') => self.block_comment(start)?,
                b'"' => self.string(start)?,
                b'0'..=b'9' => self.number(start)?,
                b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z' => self.word(start)?,
                _ => match TokenKind::punctuation(b) {
                    Some(kind) => self.push(kind, start, start + 1)?,
                    None => return Err(self.unexpected_character(start)),
                },
            }
            if first_only && !self.tokens.is_empty() {
                break;
            }
        }
        // The end-of-file token is always pushed: the bound reserves room for it.
        self.tokens.push(Token {
            kind: TokenKind::Eof,
            start: offset(self.pos),
        });
        Ok(Tokens {
            tokens: self.tokens,
            comments: self.comments,
        })
    }

    fn peek(&self, ahead: usize) -> Option<u8> {
        self.bytes.get(self.pos + ahead).copied()
    }

    /// Records a token ending at `end` and moves past it.
    fn push(&mut self, kind: TokenKind, start: usize, end: usize) -> Result<(), MoriDiagnostic> {
        if self.tokens.len() >= MAX_TOKENS - 1 {
            return Err(diagnostics::too_many_tokens(span(start, end)));
        }
        self.tokens.push(Token {
            kind,
            start: offset(start),
        });
        self.pos = end;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn push_comment(&mut self, start: usize, end: usize) {
        self.comments.push(Comment {
            start: offset(start),
            end: offset(end),
        });
        self.pos = end;
    }

    /// `//` up to, but not including, the next line break.
    fn line_comment(&mut self, start: usize) {
        let end = self.bytes[start..]
            .iter()
            .position(|&b| b == b'\r' || b == b'\n')
            .map_or(self.bytes.len(), |len| start + len);
        self.push_comment(start, end);
    }

    /// `/*` through the first `*/`. Block comments do not nest.
    fn block_comment(&mut self, start: usize) -> Result<(), MoriDiagnostic> {
        let body = start + 2;
        let Some(len) = self.source[body..].find("*/") else {
            return Err(diagnostics::unterminated_block_comment(span(start, body)));
        };
        self.push_comment(start, body + len + 2);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn string(&mut self, start: usize) -> Result<(), MoriDiagnostic> {
        let Some(end) = scan::string_end(self.bytes, start) else {
            return Err(diagnostics::unterminated_string(span(start, start + 1)));
        };
        let raw = &self.source[start..end];
        let mut decoded_len = 0;
        if let Err(error) = string::decode_with(raw, |c| decoded_len += c.len_utf8()) {
            let at = span(start + error.start, start + error.end);
            return Err(match error.kind {
                StringErrorKind::ControlCharacter('\r' | '\n') => {
                    diagnostics::string_line_break(at)
                }
                StringErrorKind::ControlCharacter(c) => {
                    diagnostics::string_control_character(at, c)
                }
                StringErrorKind::InvalidEscape => {
                    diagnostics::invalid_escape(at, at.source_text(self.source))
                }
                StringErrorKind::InvalidUnicodeEscape => diagnostics::invalid_unicode_escape(at),
                StringErrorKind::LoneSurrogate => diagnostics::lone_surrogate(at),
            });
        }
        if decoded_len > MAX_STRING_BYTES {
            return Err(diagnostics::string_too_long(span(start, end), decoded_len));
        }
        self.push(TokenKind::String, start, end)
    }

    fn number(&mut self, start: usize) -> Result<(), MoriDiagnostic> {
        let end = scan::number_end(self.bytes, start);
        let raw = &self.source[start..end];
        if let Err(error) = number::validate(raw) {
            return Err(match error {
                NumberError::LeadingZero => diagnostics::number_leading_zero(
                    span(start, end),
                    &number::without_leading_zeros(raw),
                ),
                NumberError::MisplacedUnderscore { at } => {
                    diagnostics::number_misplaced_underscore(span(start + at, start + at + 1))
                }
                NumberError::MissingFraction => {
                    diagnostics::number_missing_fraction(span(end - 1, end))
                }
                NumberError::ExtraDot { at } => {
                    diagnostics::number_extra_dot(span(start + at, start + at + 1))
                }
            });
        }
        self.push(TokenKind::Number, start, end)
    }

    /// An identifier, or a keyword when the text matches one.
    fn word(&mut self, start: usize) -> Result<(), MoriDiagnostic> {
        let end = scan::word_end(self.bytes, start);
        if end - start > MAX_IDENT_BYTES {
            return Err(diagnostics::identifier_too_long(span(start, end)));
        }
        let kind = TokenKind::keyword(&self.source[start..end]).unwrap_or(TokenKind::Ident);
        self.push(kind, start, end)
    }

    fn unexpected_character(&self, start: usize) -> MoriDiagnostic {
        let c = self.source[start..]
            .chars()
            .next()
            .expect("a character remains at the current position");
        let at = span(start, start + c.len_utf8());
        match c {
            '/' => diagnostics::division(at),
            '“' | '”' | '‘' | '’' => diagnostics::curly_quote(at),
            '\'' => diagnostics::single_quote(at),
            '_' => diagnostics::leading_underscore(at),
            c if !c.is_ascii() => diagnostics::non_ascii(at, c),
            c => diagnostics::unexpected_character(at, c),
        }
    }
}

/// Converts a byte index to an offset. Sources fit in `u32` after the bound check.
fn offset(index: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::try_from(index).expect("source offsets fit in u32")
}

fn span(start: usize, end: usize) -> Span {
    Span::new(offset(start), offset(end))
}
````

use mori_span::Span;
use soa_rs::{Soa, Soars};

use crate::scan;

/// The kind of a token. Keywords get their own kinds so the parser compares
/// tags instead of text.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum TokenKind {
    /// A name that is not a keyword: `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, at most 64 bytes.
    Ident,
    /// A canonical decimal number, such as `1_000` or `10.50`.
    Number,
    /// A JSON string literal, such as `"Midnight"`.
    String,

    // Keywords stay contiguous from `KwProfile` to `KwShareClass`; see `is_keyword`.
    KwProfile,
    KwAgreement,
    KwAction,
    KwUses,
    KwTrue,
    KwFalse,
    KwNone,
    KwSuccessOnly,

    // Declaration kinds stay contiguous from `KwDomain` to `KwShareClass`; see
    // `is_declaration_kind`.
    KwDomain,
    KwAccount,
    KwAsset,
    KwConst,
    KwIntent,
    KwObligation,
    KwPool,
    KwInstrument,
    KwObservation,
    KwPolicy,
    KwGrant,
    KwStage,
    KwEpisode,
    KwParty,
    KwShareClass,

    LBrace,
    RBrace,
    LBracket,
    RBracket,
    LParen,
    RParen,
    Colon,
    Semicolon,
    Comma,
    Eq,
    Lt,
    Gt,
    Dot,
    Plus,
    Minus,
    Star,

    Eof,
}

impl TokenKind {
    /// The keyword spelled `text`, if any.
    pub fn keyword(text: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        let kind = match text {
            "profile" => Self::KwProfile,
            "agreement" => Self::KwAgreement,
            "action" => Self::KwAction,
            "uses" => Self::KwUses,
            "true" => Self::KwTrue,
            "false" => Self::KwFalse,
            "None" => Self::KwNone,
            "SuccessOnly" => Self::KwSuccessOnly,
            "domain" => Self::KwDomain,
            "account" => Self::KwAccount,
            "asset" => Self::KwAsset,
            "const" => Self::KwConst,
            "intent" => Self::KwIntent,
            "obligation" => Self::KwObligation,
            "pool" => Self::KwPool,
            "instrument" => Self::KwInstrument,
            "observation" => Self::KwObservation,
            "policy" => Self::KwPolicy,
            "grant" => Self::KwGrant,
            "stage" => Self::KwStage,
            "episode" => Self::KwEpisode,
            "party" => Self::KwParty,
            "share_class" => Self::KwShareClass,
            _ => return None,
        };
        Some(kind)
    }

    /// The punctuation token for byte `b`, if any.
    pub fn punctuation(b: u8) -> Option<Self> {
        let kind = match b {
            b'{' => Self::LBrace,
            b'}' => Self::RBrace,
            b'[' => Self::LBracket,
            b']' => Self::RBracket,
            b'(' => Self::LParen,
            b')' => Self::RParen,
            b':' => Self::Colon,
            b';' => Self::Semicolon,
            b',' => Self::Comma,
            b'=' => Self::Eq,
            b'<' => Self::Lt,
            b'>' => Self::Gt,
            b'.' => Self::Dot,
            b'+' => Self::Plus,
            b'-' => Self::Minus,
            b'*' => Self::Star,
            _ => return None,
        };
        Some(kind)
    }

    pub fn is_keyword(self) -> bool {
        (Self::KwProfile as u8..=Self::KwShareClass as u8).contains(&(self as u8))
    }

    /// Keywords that start a declaration, such as `const` or `asset`.
    pub fn is_declaration_kind(self) -> bool {
        (Self::KwDomain as u8..=Self::KwShareClass as u8).contains(&(self as u8))
    }

    /// Identifiers and keywords. Record fields and call names accept either.
    pub fn is_word(self) -> bool {
        self == Self::Ident || self.is_keyword()
    }
}

/// A token's kind and start offset. Its end is recovered by re-scanning.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Soars)]
#[soa_derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Token {
    pub kind: TokenKind,
    pub start: u32,
}

/// A `//` or `/* */` comment, kept for the formatter.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Soars)]
#[soa_derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Comment {
    pub start: u32,
    pub end: u32,
}

/// Index of a token in [`Tokens`]. Sources hold at most 8,192 tokens.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct TokenIdx(u16);

impl TokenIdx {
    pub fn new(index: usize) -> Self {
        Self(u16::try_from(index).expect("token index exceeds u16"))
    }

    pub fn index(self) -> usize {
        usize::from(self.0)
    }
}

/// The output of [`lex`](crate::lex): every token, ending with
/// [`TokenKind::Eof`], and every comment, both in source order.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Tokens {
    pub tokens: Soa<Token>,
    pub comments: Soa<Comment>,
}

impl Tokens {
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.tokens.len()
    }

    /// Always false: a token list ends with [`TokenKind::Eof`].
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.tokens.is_empty()
    }

    pub fn kind(&self, idx: TokenIdx) -> TokenKind {
        self.tokens.kind()[idx.index()]
    }

    pub fn start(&self, idx: TokenIdx) -> u32 {
        self.tokens.start()[idx.index()]
    }

    /// The token's span, recovered by re-scanning `source` from its start.
    pub fn span(&self, idx: TokenIdx, source: &str) -> Span {
        let start = self.start(idx);
        Span::new(
            start,
            scan::token_end(self.kind(idx), source.as_bytes(), start),
        )
    }

    pub fn comment_span(&self, index: usize) -> Span {
        Span::new(self.comments.start()[index], self.comments.end()[index])
    }
}

//! Canonical number spelling.
//!
//! A number is an integer part, optionally followed by `.` and a fraction
//! part. The integer part is `0` or starts with `1`–`9`. In both parts `_` may
//! only separate two digits. This matches the reference spelling
//! `(0|[1-9][0-9]*(_[0-9]+)*)(\.[0-9]+(_[0-9]+)*)?`.

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum NumberError {
    /// The integer part has more than one digit and starts with `0`.
    LeadingZero,
    /// A `_` at this byte offset is not between two digits.
    MisplacedUnderscore { at: usize },
    /// The `.` at the end has no digits after it.
    MissingFraction,
    /// A second `.` at this byte offset.
    ExtraDot { at: usize },
}

/// Checks the spelling of a number scanned by `scan::number_end`.
pub fn validate(raw: &str) -> Result<(), NumberError> {
    let mut dots = raw.match_indices('.').map(|(at, _)| at);
    let dot = dots.next();
    if let Some(at) = dots.next() {
        return Err(NumberError::ExtraDot { at });
    }

    let integer = &raw[..dot.unwrap_or(raw.len())];
    if integer.len() > 1 && integer.starts_with('0') {
        return Err(NumberError::LeadingZero);
    }
    check_underscores(integer, 0)?;

    if let Some(dot) = dot {
        let fraction = &raw[dot + 1..];
        if fraction.is_empty() {
            return Err(NumberError::MissingFraction);
        }
        check_underscores(fraction, dot + 1)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `part` contains only digits and `_` and starts at `offset` in the number.
fn check_underscores(part: &str, offset: usize) -> Result<(), NumberError> {
    let bytes = part.as_bytes();
    for (i, &b) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {
        let between_digits = i > 0
            && bytes[i - 1].is_ascii_digit()
            && bytes.get(i + 1).is_some_and(u8::is_ascii_digit);
        if b == b'_' && !between_digits {
            return Err(NumberError::MisplacedUnderscore { at: offset + i });
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The number with redundant leading zeros removed, for suggestions.
pub fn without_leading_zeros(raw: &str) -> String {
    let (integer, rest) = raw.split_at(raw.find('.').unwrap_or(raw.len()));
    let trimmed = integer.trim_start_matches(['0', '_']);
    let integer = if trimmed.is_empty() { "0" } else { trimmed };
    format!("{integer}{rest}")
}
````
